benilla_world::shaderssrccrates\benilla-world\src\shaders.rsshaders/sky_vertex.wgsl// The vertex stage of every sky draw: bevy 0.18.1's `mesh.wgsl` vertex verbatim, minus the morph
\n// targets and skinning no sky mesh has, plus one line pinning clip z to the far plane. A
\n// `MaterialExtension` replaces the whole stage, so this copy must track bevy's on upgrades.
\n// The reference draws its sky first in a back depth slice and the world paints over it; here the
\n// sky draws after the world, so the depth test does that job. The pin is per vertex because a
\n// fragment depth write would disable early-Z.
\n#import bevy_pbr::{
\n    mesh_functions,
\n    forward_io::{Vertex, VertexOutput},
\n    view_transformations::position_world_to_clip,
\n/// Reverse-Z "infinitely far": clip z = 0 gives NDC depth exactly 0.0 whatever w, so under bevy's
\n/// `GreaterEqual` test a sky fragment passes only where the depth buffer still holds its clear 0.0.
\nconst SKY_FAR_CLIP_Z: f32 = 0.0;
\n@vertex
\nfn vertex(vertex_no_morph: Vertex) -> VertexOutput {
\n    var out: VertexOutput;
\n    var vertex = vertex_no_morph;
\n    let mesh_world_from_local = mesh_functions::get_world_from_local(vertex_no_morph.instance_index);
\n    // Use vertex_no_morph.instance_index instead of vertex.instance_index to work around a wgpu dx12 bug.
\n    // See https://github.com/gfx-rs/naga/issues/2416 .
\n    var world_from_local = mesh_world_from_local;
\n#ifdef VERTEX_NORMALS
\n    out.world_normal = mesh_functions::mesh_normal_local_to_world(
\n        vertex.normal,
\n        // Use vertex_no_morph.instance_index instead of vertex.instance_index to work around a wgpu dx12 bug.
\n        // See https://github.com/gfx-rs/naga/issues/2416
\n        vertex_no_morph.instance_index
\n#endif
\n#ifdef VERTEX_POSITIONS
\n    out.world_position = mesh_functions::mesh_position_local_to_world(world_from_local, vec4<f32>(vertex.position, 1.0));
\n    out.position = position_world_to_clip(out.world_position.xyz);
\n    // The one line not from bevy: the far-plane pin.
\n    out.position.z = SKY_FAR_CLIP_Z;
\n#endif
\n#ifdef VERTEX_UVS_A
\n    out.uv = vertex.uv;
\n#endif
\n#ifdef VERTEX_UVS_B
\n    out.uv_b = vertex.uv_b;
\n#endif
\n#ifdef VERTEX_TANGENTS
\n    out.world_tangent = mesh_functions::mesh_tangent_local_to_world(
\n        world_from_local,
\n        vertex.tangent,
\n        // Use vertex_no_morph.instance_index instead of vertex.instance_index to work around a wgpu dx12 bug.
\n        // See https://github.com/gfx-rs/naga/issues/2416
\n        vertex_no_morph.instance_index
\n#endif
\n#ifdef VERTEX_COLORS
\n    out.color = vertex.color;
\n#endif
\n#ifdef VERTEX_OUTPUT_INSTANCE_INDEX
\n    // Use vertex_no_morph.instance_index instead of vertex.instance_index to work around a wgpu dx12 bug.
\n    // See https://github.com/gfx-rs/naga/issues/2416
\n    out.instance_index = vertex_no_morph.instance_index;
\n#endif
\n#ifdef VISIBILITY_RANGE_DITHER
\n    out.visibility_range_dither = mesh_functions::get_visibility_range_dither_level(
\n        vertex_no_morph.instance_index, mesh_world_from_local[3]);
\n#endif
\n    return out;
shaders/sky.wgsl// The sky-dome gradient (`SkyExt`): the five Light.dbc SkyColor stops at the reference's ring
\n// elevations, then the fog colour at and below the horizon (`0x6d0d10`, `0x6d0f50`), interpolated
\n// per fragment by elevation. Depth is the far pin in `sky_vertex.wgsl`; this writes colour only.
\n#import bevy_pbr::{
\n    forward_io::VertexOutput,
\n    mesh_view_bindings::view,
\nstruct SkyColors {
\n    sky0: vec4<f32>, // zenith (90°)
\n    sky1: vec4<f32>, // 16.8°
\n    sky2: vec4<f32>, // 9.8°
\n    sky3: vec4<f32>, // 3.7°
\n    sky4: vec4<f32>, // 1.8°
\n    fog: vec4<f32>,  // horizon (0°) and below: LightIntBand row 7
\n    warp: vec4<f32>, // x = dawn/dusk warp strength S (0 = off), y = sun azimuth (rad), zw reserved
\n@group(#{MATERIAL_BIND_GROUP}) @binding(100) var<uniform> sky: SkyColors;
\n// Glow `g` for a sun-relative azimuth phase, sampled linearly like `0x6d0f50` from the reference's
\n// six-keyframe wrap-around table at `0xce9af8` (written by `0x6ce210`); 0.125 is the sun bearing.
\nfn azimuth_glow(phase: f32) -> f32 {
\n    let p = fract(phase);
\n    if (p < 0.125) { return mix(0.0, 1.0, (p + 0.125) / 0.25); } // wrap 0.875(g0)→1.125(g1)
\n    else if (p < 0.375) { return mix(1.0, 0.0, (p - 0.125) / 0.25); }
\n    else if (p < 0.5) { return mix(0.0, -0.5, (p - 0.375) / 0.125); }
\n    else if (p < 0.625) { return mix(-0.5, -0.7, (p - 0.5) / 0.125); }
\n    else if (p < 0.75) { return mix(-0.7, -0.5, (p - 0.625) / 0.125); }
\n    else if (p < 0.875) { return mix(-0.5, 0.0, (p - 0.75) / 0.125); }
\n    else { return mix(0.0, 1.0, (p - 0.875) / 0.25); } // wrap 0.875(g0)→1.125(g1)
\n// One mid-ring's warped colour for glow `g` (`0x6d0f50`): `S^2` is the prepass S nested in the
\n// per-segment S, and 0.7 is the constant at `0x7ffd7c`.
\nfn warp_one(base: vec3<f32>, g: f32, s: f32) -> vec3<f32> {
\n    let s2 = s * s;
\n        return mix(base, sky.sky1.rgb, (1.0 - g) * s2);
\n    return mix(mix(base, sky.sky1.rgb, s), sky.sky0.rgb, 0.7 * (-g) * s2);
\n@fragment
\nfn fragment(in: VertexOutput) -> @location(0) vec4<f32> {
\n    let dir = normalize(in.world_position.xyz - view.world_position.xyz);
\n    let elev = degrees(asin(clamp(dir.y, -1.0, 1.0))); // −90..90, 0 = horizon
\n    // Dawn/dusk warp (`0x6d0f50`): only the four mid rings, never the apex or the fog rim, and
\n    // never brighter. The reference bakes it per vertex at 24 azimuth segments and interpolates,
\n    // hence the lerp of two segments; `+ 0.125` puts the sun bearing at glow phase 0.125.
\n    var s1 = sky.sky1.rgb;
\n    var s2c = sky.sky2.rgb;
\n    var s3 = sky.sky3.rgb;
\n    var s4 = sky.sky4.rgb;
\n    let warp_s = sky.warp.x;
\n    if (warp_s > 0.0) {
\n        let az = fract((atan2(dir.z, dir.x) - sky.warp.y) / 6.2831853 + 0.125);
\n        let seg = az * 24.0; // 24 azimuth segments, like the dome vertices
\n        let s0 = floor(seg);
\n        let f = seg - s0;
\n        let g0 = azimuth_glow(s0 / 24.0);
\n        let g1 = azimuth_glow((s0 + 1.0) / 24.0);
\n        s1 = mix(warp_one(sky.sky1.rgb, g0, warp_s), warp_one(sky.sky1.rgb, g1, warp_s), f);
\n        s2c = mix(warp_one(sky.sky2.rgb, g0, warp_s), warp_one(sky.sky2.rgb, g1, warp_s), f);
\n        s3 = mix(warp_one(sky.sky3.rgb, g0, warp_s), warp_one(sky.sky3.rgb, g1, warp_s), f);
\n        s4 = mix(warp_one(sky.sky4.rgb, g0, warp_s), warp_one(sky.sky4.rgb, g1, warp_s), f);
\n    // Elevation gradient, linear between rings like the reference's Gouraud-shaded dome.
\n    var col: vec3<f32>;
\n    if (elev <= 0.0) {
\n        col = sky.fog.rgb; // horizon and below = fog colour (row 7), unwarped
\n    } else if (elev < 1.8) {
\n        col = mix(sky.fog.rgb, s4, elev / 1.8);
\n    } else if (elev < 3.7) {
\n        col = mix(s4, s3, (elev - 1.8) / (3.7 - 1.8));
\n    } else if (elev < 9.8) {
\n        col = mix(s3, s2c, (elev - 3.7) / (9.8 - 3.7));
\n    } else if (elev < 16.8) {
\n        col = mix(s2c, s1, (elev - 9.8) / (16.8 - 9.8));
\n    } else {
\n        col = mix(s1, sky.sky0.rgb, (elev - 16.8) / (90.0 - 16.8)); // warped ring1 to the raw apex
\n    // Raw gamma out: the reference draws the sky as raw DBC bytes, sRGB off (`0x6d4940`).
\n    let rgb = col;
\n    return vec4<f32>(rgb, 1.0);
shaders/star.wgsl// Night-sky stars (`Stars.m2`): white `Stars.blp` dots blended as premultiplied white in gamma
\n// space, as the reference blends them. Depth is the far pin in `sky_vertex.wgsl`.
\n#import bevy_pbr::{
\n    pbr_fragment::pbr_input_from_standard_material,
\n    forward_io::VertexOutput,
\n@fragment
\nfn fragment(in: VertexOutput, @builtin(front_facing) is_front: bool) -> @location(0) vec4<f32> {
\n    let pbr_input = pbr_input_from_standard_material(in, is_front);
\n    let a = pbr_input.material.base_color.a; // texel alpha × the per-frame `base_color` alpha
\n    return vec4<f32>(vec3<f32>(a), a); // premultiplied white, raw gamma
shaders/cloud.wgsl// The cloud dome. Its colour is CPU-side as in the reference: the kernel's `0x6cfb00` port builds
\n// the image the reference binds as its texture (`0x58ac70`). This stage applies the dome's rim
\n// fade (`0x6d0530`) and blends the raw gamma texels premultiplied. Depth is the far pin in
\n// `sky_vertex.wgsl`.
\n#import bevy_pbr::forward_io::VertexOutput
\n@group(#{MATERIAL_BIND_GROUP}) @binding(100) var cloud_tex: texture_2d<f32>;
\n@group(#{MATERIAL_BIND_GROUP}) @binding(101) var cloud_samp: sampler;
\n@fragment
\nfn fragment(in: VertexOutput) -> @location(0) vec4<f32> {
\n    let texel = textureSample(cloud_tex, cloud_samp, in.uv);
\n    var a = texel.a;
\n#ifdef VERTEX_COLORS
\n    a *= in.color.a; // the dome's rim fade (ring alphas)
\n#endif
\n    // Premultiplied gamma blend; the RGB is already the reference's byte math.
\n    return vec4<f32>(texel.rgb * a, a);
shaders/celestial.wgsl// Celestial discs (sun, white moon, moon02) and their glares, blended in gamma space as the
\n// reference blends onto gamma bytes. Discs take its horizon clip and fade (`0x6d1960`): clipped
\n// at height 0 with alpha 0 there, `clamp(2.5 * height, 0, 1)` in the 0.4-unit band above
\n// (`0x6d1ac5`), the colour's alpha byte beyond. Glares skip the clip (`0x7e57e0`) and add,
\n// saturating, like the reference's SRC_ALPHA, ONE blend (`0x7e5a16`). Depth is the far pin in
\n// `sky_vertex.wgsl`.
\n#import bevy_pbr::{
\n    pbr_fragment::pbr_input_from_standard_material,
\n    pbr_functions::alpha_discard,
\n    forward_io::VertexOutput,
\n    mesh_view_bindings::view,
\n// `CelestialExt::fade`: `.x` the ramp slope in sin-elevation (`2.5 * height` at the reference's
\n// radius 12 is `30 * y`), `.y` the brightness on RGB only, `.z` 0 for a disc and 1 for a glare,
\n// `.w` the colour's alpha byte above the band, 0 for moon02 in clear weather (no writer).
\n@group(#{MATERIAL_BIND_GROUP}) @binding(100) var<uniform> celestial: vec4<f32>;
\n// The disc quad's vertical span in sin-elevation, `.x` bottom edge and `.y` top edge, per frame.
\n@group(#{MATERIAL_BIND_GROUP}) @binding(101) var<uniform> span: vec4<f32>;
\n// The reference's per-vertex alpha at sin-elevation `y`: the ramp inside the band, the byte above.
\nfn vertex_alpha(y: f32) -> f32 {
\n    let ramp = y * celestial.x;
\n    return select(celestial.w, clamp(ramp, 0.0, 1.0), ramp < 1.0);
\nfn linear_to_srgb(c: vec3<f32>) -> vec3<f32> {
\n    let lo = c * 12.92;
\n    let hi = 1.055 * pow(max(c, vec3<f32>(0.0)), vec3<f32>(1.0 / 2.4)) - 0.055;
\n    return select(hi, lo, c <= vec3<f32>(0.0031308));
\n@fragment
\nfn fragment(in: VertexOutput, @builtin(front_facing) is_front: bool) -> @location(0) vec4<f32> {
\n    var pbr_input = pbr_input_from_standard_material(in, is_front);
\n    let base = alpha_discard(pbr_input.material, pbr_input.material.base_color);
\n    var a = base.a;
\n    if celestial.z < 0.5 {
\n        // Disc: the vertex rule, interpolated from the clipped bottom edge to the top. The
\n        // reference's GEQUAL 1/255 alpha test needs no discard: zero alpha adds nothing here.
\n        let dir = normalize(in.world_position.xyz - view.world_position.xyz);
\n        let y = dir.y;
\n        } else {
\n            let y_bot = max(span.x, 0.0); // the horizon cut, or the bottom edge above it
\n            let a_bot = vertex_alpha(y_bot);
\n            let a_top = vertex_alpha(span.y);
\n            let t = clamp((y - y_bot) / max(span.y - y_bot, 1e-6), 0.0, 1.0);
\n            a *= mix(a_bot, a_top, t);
\n    // `base.rgb` arrives linear (Bevy decodes the sRGB texture); the target takes gamma values.
\n    let gamma = linear_to_srgb(base.rgb);
\n    if celestial.z >= 0.5 {
\n        // Glare: alpha 0 under `AlphaMode::Add` gives `dst + gamma * a`, `a` the flare envelope.
\n        return vec4<f32>(gamma * a * celestial.y, 0.0);
\n    // Disc: premultiplied gamma under `AlphaMode::Premultiplied`.
\n    return vec4<f32>(gamma * a * celestial.y, a);
shaders/ffx_glow.wgsl// FFXGlow, the reference's full-screen glow (`FFXGlow.bls`, `FFXGauss4.bls`):
\n//   blur = Gauss4(Gauss4(Box4(scene → ¼), horizontal), vertical)
\n//   out  = lerp(screen, blur, z) + w · blur²
\n// `w` is the zone's LightParams glow weight, `z` the drunk or underwater haze mix. Tap offsets
\n// count source texels from texel-centre UVs, with no half-texel shift. The math runs on gamma
\n// bytes, and every scene read clamps to 1.0 because the float target does not saturate.
\n#import bevy_core_pipeline::fullscreen_vertex_shader::FullscreenVertexOutput
\n@group(0) @binding(0) var in_tex: texture_2d<f32>;
\n@group(0) @binding(1) var in_samp: sampler;
\n// Combine-pass bindings, unbound in the downsample and blur passes.
\n@group(0) @binding(2) var blur_tex: texture_2d<f32>;
\nstruct FfxCombine {
\n    // x = zone glow weight `w` (both combines), y = FFXDeath gate (1 while a ghost, no ramp),
\n    // z = haze mix, w = deband dither on.
\n    lane: vec4<f32>,
\n    // xy = the GlowWave phases `(t mod 3174)/3174` and `(t mod 2805)/2805`, t in ms; zw unused.
\n    wave: vec4<f32>,
\n@group(0) @binding(3) var<uniform> ffx: FfxCombine;
\n// The 128×128 wave LUT and its repeat sampler: bound on every combine, sampled only underwater.
\n@group(0) @binding(4) var wave_tex: texture_2d<f32>;
\n@group(0) @binding(5) var wave_samp: sampler;
\n// Box4, full → ¼: four bilinear taps over a 4×4 footprint (`0xce89cc`), each clamped to 1.0 like
\n// the reference's byte target; an unclamped super-white would square into a hard glow disc.
\n@fragment
\nfn fs_downsample(in: FullscreenVertexOutput) -> @location(0) vec4<f32> {
\n    let texel = 1.0 / vec2<f32>(textureDimensions(in_tex));
\n    let one = vec4<f32>(1.0);
\n    return (min(textureSample(in_tex, in_samp, in.uv + vec2<f32>(-1.5, -1.5) * texel), one)
\n        + min(textureSample(in_tex, in_samp, in.uv + vec2<f32>(0.5, -1.5) * texel), one)
\n        + min(textureSample(in_tex, in_samp, in.uv + vec2<f32>(0.5, 0.5) * texel), one)
\n        + min(textureSample(in_tex, in_samp, in.uv + vec2<f32>(-1.5, 0.5) * texel), one))
\n// Gauss4: taps at ±0.5 and ±2.5 source texels (0x6cad10), weights from FFXGauss4.bls.
\nfn gauss4(uv: vec2<f32>, axis: vec2<f32>) -> vec4<f32> {
\n    let texel = axis / vec2<f32>(textureDimensions(in_tex));
\n    return textureSample(in_tex, in_samp, uv - 2.5 * texel) * 0.125
\n        + textureSample(in_tex, in_samp, uv - 0.5 * texel) * 0.375
\n        + textureSample(in_tex, in_samp, uv + 0.5 * texel) * 0.375
\n        + textureSample(in_tex, in_samp, uv + 2.5 * texel) * 0.125;
\n@fragment
\nfn fs_gauss_h(in: FullscreenVertexOutput) -> @location(0) vec4<f32> {
\n    return gauss4(in.uv, vec2<f32>(1.0, 0.0));
\n@fragment
\nfn fs_gauss_v(in: FullscreenVertexOutput) -> @location(0) vec4<f32> {
\n    return gauss4(in.uv, vec2<f32>(0.0, 1.0));
\nfn srgb_to_linear(c: vec3<f32>) -> vec3<f32> {
\n    let lo = c / 12.92;
\n    let hi = pow((c + vec3<f32>(0.055)) / 1.055, vec3<f32>(2.4));
\n    return select(hi, lo, c <= vec3<f32>(0.04045));
\n// Deviation, opt-in (`WOW_DITHER=1`): a dither against banding, which the reference's 8-bit
\n// framebuffer lacks. The hash is Bevy's `screen_space_dither`, copied here because Bevy applies
\n// it only in the tonemapping pass that `Tonemapping::None` skips.
\nfn screen_space_dither(frag_coord: vec2<f32>) -> vec3<f32> {
\n    var dither = vec3<f32>(dot(vec2<f32>(171.0, 231.0), frag_coord)).xxx;
\n    dither = fract(dither.rgb / vec3<f32>(103.0, 71.0, 97.0));
\n    return (dither - vec3<f32>(0.5)) / 255.0;
\n// The combine's exit: dither in gamma space, where the present-encode rounds, then the frame's
\n// one decode, which the sRGB present-encode reverses byte-exactly; none under `GAMMA_OUT`.
\nfn combine_out(outg: vec3<f32>, alpha: f32, frag_coord: vec2<f32>) -> vec4<f32> {
\n    let dithered = clamp(
\n        outg + screen_space_dither(frag_coord) * step(0.5, ffx.lane.w),
\n        vec3<f32>(0.0),
\n        vec3<f32>(1.0),
\n#ifdef GAMMA_OUT
\n    // The UI camera's ground pass stores premultiplied bytes like `ui_quad.wgsl`; the lane decodes.
\n    return vec4<f32>(dithered * alpha, alpha);
\n#else
\n    return vec4<f32>(srgb_to_linear(dithered), alpha);
\n#endif
\n// Both combines, at the plain or the warped UV; `frag_coord` stays unwarped for the dither.
\nfn combine_body(uv: vec2<f32>, frag_coord: vec2<f32>) -> vec4<f32> {
\n    let scene = textureSample(in_tex, in_samp, uv);
\n    // Clamped like the downsample taps: the screen term must saturate before the glow add.
\n    let sg = clamp(scene.rgb, vec3<f32>(0.0), vec3<f32>(1.0));
\n    let bg = max(textureSample(blur_tex, in_samp, uv).rgb, vec3<f32>(0.0));
\n    // Scene alpha passes through; only the transparent-clear create booth reads it.
\n    if ffx.lane.y > 0.0 {
\n        // FFXDeath replaces the glow while a ghost, unhazed (one pass slot, `[0xce8bb4]`). The
\n        // 0.144 blue weight is as shipped; the tint is packed at `0x6cb930`.
\n        let glowed = sg + ffx.lane.x * bg * bg;
\n        let luma = clamp(dot(glowed, vec3<f32>(0.299, 0.587, 0.144)), 0.0, 1.0);
\n        let p = clamp(4.0 * luma * (1.0 - luma), 0.0, 1.0);
\n        let ghost_tint = vec3<f32>(83.0, 147.0, 168.0) / 255.0; // 0x5393A8
\n        let outg = min(vec3<f32>(luma) + ghost_tint * p, vec3<f32>(1.0));
\n        return combine_out(outg, scene.a, frag_coord);
\n    // The haze fades toward the blur before the glow add; z is the larger of the drunk fraction
\n    // and 84/255 while submerged.
\n    let hazed = mix(sg, min(bg, vec3<f32>(1.0)), ffx.lane.z);
\n    let outg = min(hazed + ffx.lane.x * bg * bg, vec3<f32>(1.0));
\n    return combine_out(outg, scene.a, frag_coord);
\n@fragment
\nfn fs_combine(in: FullscreenVertexOutput) -> @location(0) vec4<f32> {
\n    return combine_body(in.uv, in.position.xy);
\n// FFXGlowWave, the warp the reference runs instead of FFXGlow while the eye is in any liquid
\n// (`0x6cc630`, `0x6cb310`): the same combine, both texcoords displaced by a 128×128 sine LUT. The
\n// reference's per-vertex wave texcoord (`0x7bca80`) is affine in the screen UV, so per fragment
\n// is exact: uv' = uv · R(10°) · S(W/128, 0.88·H/128) · T(p1, p2), fixed to screen pixels.
\nconst WAVE_ROT_RAD: f32 = 0.174532925; // 10°, the reference's rotation row
\nconst WAVE_LUT_EDGE: f32 = 128.0; // the LUT is 128×128 texels ([0xce89a0])
\nconst WAVE_V_SCALE: f32 = 0.88; // [0xce89c0]: the v axis only; u's scale is 1.0
\nconst WAVE_AMPLITUDE_PX: f32 = 3.0; // full-res pixels, both samples
\n// The warp's screen-UV offset in UV units; `screen` is the full-res scene size in pixels.
\nfn wave_offset(uv: vec2<f32>, screen: vec2<f32>) -> vec2<f32> {
\n    let c = cos(WAVE_ROT_RAD);
\n    let s = sin(WAVE_ROT_RAD);
\n    let scale = vec2<f32>(screen.x, WAVE_V_SCALE * screen.y) / WAVE_LUT_EDGE;
\n    let tex = vec2<f32>(c * uv.x - s * uv.y, s * uv.x + c * uv.y) * scale + ffx.wave.xy;
\n    // Sampled, not evaluated: the reference's sine is a filtered LUT. The sampler must repeat,
\n    // as the texcoord spans about 10 cycles; the unbias matches the shipped ps_2_0 shader.
\n    let d = (textureSample(wave_tex, wave_samp, tex).rg - vec2<f32>(0.5)) * 2.0;
\n    return d * WAVE_AMPLITUDE_PX / screen;
\n@fragment
\nfn fs_combine_wave(in: FullscreenVertexOutput) -> @location(0) vec4<f32> {
\n    let screen = vec2<f32>(textureDimensions(in_tex));
\n    return combine_body(in.uv + wave_offset(in.uv, screen), in.position.xy);
shaders/wow_effect.wgsl// The effect-lane pass (particles, ribbons, decals, water foam, precipitation): texture bytes,
\n// never decoded on sample, times the authored track colour in gamma space, as the reference
\n// multiplies them. The output stays gamma; the FFXGlow combine decodes the frame once.
\n// Blend variants, one shader def per EffectBlend:
\n// - BLEND_ADD:      (rgb·α, 0) under (One, 1−srcα), the reference's `src·α` byte add.
\n// - BLEND_ALPHA:    straight (rgb, α) under standard alpha blending.
\n// - BLEND_OPAQUE:   (rgb, 1) with blending off.
\n// - BLEND_ALPHAKEY: BLEND_OPAQUE behind the alpha test (EGxRs id 0x08), a discard below 224/255.
\n// - BLEND_MULTIPLY: (rgb·α, α) under (Dst, 1−srcα) = `dst·lerp(1, rgb, α)`, the blob shadow's
\n//   modulate-with-fade and ModelBlend::Mod at α = 1.
\n// - BLEND_MOD2X:    (rgb, 1) under (Dst, Src) = `2·src·dst`, rain's state; reads no alpha.
\n#import bevy_render::view::View
\n// Prefix of `lighting::global_light`'s buffer; keep in sync with wow_model.wgsl's copy.
\nstruct WowLight {
\n    light_ambient: vec4<f32>,
\n    light_diffuse: vec4<f32>,
\n    light_sun: vec4<f32>,
\n    light_spec: vec4<f32>,
\n    fog_color: vec4<f32>,  // rgb row-7 fog (gamma); w = enable (>0.5)
\n    fog_params: vec4<f32>, // x=start y=end z=linear-lighting A/B flag w=farclip wall
\n    sh_c10_r: vec4<f32>,
\n    sh_c10_g: vec4<f32>,
\n    sh_c10_b: vec4<f32>,
\n    sh_c13_r: vec4<f32>,
\n    sh_c13_g: vec4<f32>,
\n    sh_c13_b: vec4<f32>,
\n    sh_c16: vec4<f32>,
\n    _water: array<vec4<f32>, 4>,
\n    grade: vec4<f32>,
\n@group(0) @binding(0) var<uniform> view: View;
\n@group(1) @binding(0) var effect_texture: texture_2d<f32>;
\n@group(1) @binding(1) var effect_sampler: sampler;
\n@group(1) @binding(2) var<storage, read> wow_light: WowLight;
\n// Per-draw params. `fog`: x the fog colour policy, `0x70baf0`'s per-blend table (0 off for file
\n// flag 0x8, 1 scene, 2 black for Add, 3 white for Mod, 4 grey for Mod2x); y rain's forced fog, zw
\n// its start and end. `clip`: the target rect in pixels (min.xy, max.xy), the whole target when
\n// z <= x; the reference clips a UI model to its widget's viewport, and model panes share an atlas.
\nstruct EffectParams {
\n    fog: vec4<f32>,
\n    clip: vec4<f32>,
\n@group(1) @binding(3) var<uniform> wow_params: EffectParams;
\n// The rain pass's forced fog colour: 0x80808080 → grey (render-state 0x0d).
\nconst RAIN_FOG_GREY: vec3<f32> = vec3<f32>(0.50196078, 0.50196078, 0.50196078);
\n#ifdef SPRITE_FLAKE
\n// One snow flake per instance (`precip::render::push_flakes`): xyz its camera-relative centre,
\n// w its alpha. Six vertices make its screen-aligned quad.
\nstruct Vertex {
\n    @builtin(vertex_index) corner: u32,
\n    @location(0) flake: vec4<f32>,
\n#else
\n#ifdef SPRITE_STREAK
\n// One rain streak per instance (`precip::render::push_streaks`): the camera-relative head, the
\n// unit anti-velocity and the tilted tail offset. Three vertices make its triangle.
\nstruct Vertex {
\n    @builtin(vertex_index) corner: u32,
\n    @location(0) head: vec4<f32>,
\n    @location(1) anti: vec4<f32>,
\n    @location(2) tail: vec4<f32>,
\n#else
\nstruct Vertex {
\n    // Camera-relative for f32 precision (absolute verts through `clip_from_world` shear thin
\n    // geometry far from the origin), except decals under DECAL_WORLD_CLIP, which arrive absolute.
\n    @location(0) position: vec3<f32>,
\n    @location(1) uv: vec2<f32>,
\n    @location(2) color: vec4<f32>,    // raw authored gamma RGBA; α is the blend weight
\n#endif
\n#endif
\n#ifdef SPRITE_STREAK
\n// glam's `normalize_or`: the fallback where the vector has no direction.
\nfn normalize_or(v: vec3<f32>, fallback: vec3<f32>) -> vec3<f32> {
\n    let len = length(v);
\n    if (len > 0.0) {
\n        return v / len;
\n    return fallback;
\n#endif
\nstruct VertexOutput {
\n    @builtin(position) clip_position: vec4<f32>,
\n    @location(0) uv: vec2<f32>,
\n    @location(1) color: vec4<f32>,
\n    // Planar eye-Z for fog and the farclip wall, positive in front of the camera.
\n    @location(2) view_z: f32,
\n@vertex
\nfn vertex(v: Vertex) -> VertexOutput {
\n    var out: VertexOutput;
\n#ifdef SPRITE_FLAKE
\n    // The quad's corners in the stream's perimeter order (bl, br, tr, tl), as the triangles
\n    // [0, 1, 2] and [0, 2, 3].
\n    var corner = v.corner;
\n    if (corner == 3u) {
\n        corner = 0u;
\n    } else if (corner > 3u) {
\n        corner = corner - 2u;
\n    let sx = select(-1.0, 1.0, corner == 1u || corner == 2u);
\n    let sy = select(-1.0, 1.0, corner >= 2u);
\n    // `snowpoint.bls`'s size in era pixels off the radial distance, then pixels to world at the
\n    // flake's view depth: half-extent `px·z·tan(fovY/2)/SNOW_PX_REF_HEIGHT`, never the live
\n    // viewport height. `clip_from_view[1][1]` is `1/tan(fovY/2)`.
\n    let rel = v.flake.xyz;
\n    let z = dot(rel, -view.world_from_view[2].xyz);
\n    let px = max(
\n        bitcast<f32>(#{SNOW_PX_AT_EYE}u)
\n            * clamp(1.0 - bitcast<f32>(#{SNOW_PX_FALLOFF}u) * length(rel), 0.0, 1.0),
\n        bitcast<f32>(#{SNOW_PX_MIN}u),
\n    let half = px * z / view.clip_from_view[1][1] / bitcast<f32>(#{SNOW_PX_REF_HEIGHT}u);
\n    let position = rel
\n        + view.world_from_view[0].xyz * (sx * half)
\n        + view.world_from_view[1].xyz * (sy * half);
\n    let uv = vec2<f32>(select(0.0, 1.0, sx > 0.0), select(1.0, 0.0, sy > 0.0));
\n    let color = vec4<f32>(1.0, 1.0, 1.0, v.flake.w);
\n#else
\n#ifdef SPRITE_STREAK
\n    // Base `head ∓ right` with `right` across the view of the fall, apex `head + tail`.
\n    let head = v.head.xyz;
\n    let to_cam = normalize_or(-head, vec3<f32>(1.0, 0.0, 0.0));
\n    let right = normalize_or(cross(to_cam, v.anti.xyz), vec3<f32>(1.0, 0.0, 0.0))
\n        * bitcast<f32>(#{STREAK_HALF_W}u);
\n    var position = head - right;
\n    var uv = vec2<f32>(0.0, 1.0);
\n    if (v.corner == 1u) {
\n        position = head + right;
\n        uv = vec2<f32>(1.0, 1.0);
\n    } else if (v.corner == 2u) {
\n        position = head + v.tail.xyz;
\n        uv = vec2<f32>(0.5, 0.0);
\n    let color = vec4<f32>(1.0);
\n#else
\n    let position = v.position;
\n    let uv = v.uv;
\n    let color = v.color;
\n#endif
\n#endif
\n#ifdef DECAL_WORLD_CLIP
\n    // Decals (raster_bias ≠ 0) take absolute verts through the world meshes' `clip_from_world`:
\n    // their depth must tie the ground within the raster bias, and the cam-relative route rounds
\n    // differently by more than that at world-scale coordinates.
\n    out.clip_position = view.clip_from_world * vec4<f32>(position, 1.0);
\n    // Eye-Z via the full affine transform; its rounding is yard-scale and harmless.
\n    out.view_z = -(view.view_from_world * vec4<f32>(position, 1.0)).z;
\n#else
\n    // Cam-relative verts: view_from_world is [R | −R·cam] and the rebase already subtracted cam,
\n    // so only the rotation applies.
\n    let view_pos = mat3x3<f32>(
\n        view.view_from_world[0].xyz,
\n        view.view_from_world[1].xyz,
\n        view.view_from_world[2].xyz,
\n    ) * position;
\n    out.clip_position = view.clip_from_view * vec4<f32>(view_pos, 1.0);
\n    out.view_z = -view_pos.z;
\n#endif
\n    out.uv = uv;
\n    out.color = color;
\n    return out;
\n@fragment
\nfn fragment(in: VertexOutput) -> @location(0) vec4<f32> {
\n    // The target-rect clip; `@builtin(position)` is the framebuffer pixel, a UI tile's atlas texel.
\n    if (wow_params.clip.z > wow_params.clip.x) {
\n        let p = in.clip_position.xy;
\n        if (p.x < wow_params.clip.x || p.y < wow_params.clip.y
\n            || p.x > wow_params.clip.z || p.y > wow_params.clip.w) {
\n            discard;
\n    // `$WOW_PARTICLE_FLAT` debug instrument: solid magenta, no inputs.
\n#ifdef WOW_PARTICLE_FLAT
\n    return vec4<f32>(1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0);
\n#else
\n    // The hard farclip wall (the live `farclip`, 177 to 777 yd): the reference's far plane clips
\n    // effects and ours is farther, so every world shader discards. The fog ends by the farclip, so
\n    // this cuts only fog.
\n    if (wow_light.fog_params.w > 0.0 && in.view_z > wow_light.fog_params.w) {
\n        discard;
\n    // Texture bytes × authored vertex colour in gamma space; `view.mip_bias` is the render-scale
\n    // LOD compensation, 0.0 at native and above.
\n    let c = textureSampleBias(effect_texture, effect_sampler, in.uv, view.mip_bias) * in.color;
\n#ifdef BLEND_ALPHAKEY
\n    // The fixed-function alpha test (EGxRs id 0x08, `glAlphaFunc(GL_GEQUAL, ref/255)`): `0x70c256`
\n    // sets ref = round(instanceAlpha × 224), 224 at full alpha, and `c.a` is the reference's
\n    // fragment alpha (texture α × track α, GL_MODULATE). GEQUAL passes at the ref.
\n        discard;
\n#endif
\n    var rgb = c.rgb;
\n#ifdef EFFECT_LIT
\n    // Scene lighting (EGxRs id 0x0e, `0x70d8b0`) when the emitter clears the unlit flag 0x1 and
\n    // its blend is not Mod or Mod2x (`0x70bb00`): the fixed-function matte with N = world up for
\n    // the whole draw, as `0x7b3fd0` takes the normal from view row 2 and `0x71bce0` moves the
\n    // light into that frame, so N·L holds as the camera orbits. Bevy +Y is WoW +Z.
\n    let L = -normalize(wow_light.light_sun.xyz);
\n    let N = vec3<f32>(0.0, 1.0, 0.0);
\n    let lit = clamp(
\n        wow_light.light_ambient.rgb + wow_light.light_diffuse.rgb * max(dot(N, L), 0.0),
\n        vec3<f32>(0.0),
\n        vec3<f32>(1.0),
\n    rgb = rgb * lit;
\n#endif
\n    // Scene fog: the world's linear fog (same start and end, planar eye-Z) in gamma space before
\n    // the blend; only its colour follows the per-blend policy in `wow_params.fog.x`.
\n    if (wow_light.fog_color.w > 0.5 && wow_params.fog.x > 0.5) {
\n        let denom = max(wow_light.fog_params.y - wow_light.fog_params.x, 0.001);
\n        let factor = clamp((wow_light.fog_params.y - in.view_z) / denom, 0.0, 1.0);
\n        var fog_rgb = wow_light.fog_color.xyz;
\n        if (wow_params.fog.x > 1.5 && wow_params.fog.x < 2.5) { fog_rgb = vec3<f32>(0.0); }
\n        else if (wow_params.fog.x > 2.5 && wow_params.fog.x < 3.5) { fog_rgb = vec3<f32>(1.0); }
\n        else if (wow_params.fog.x > 3.5) { fog_rgb = RAIN_FOG_GREY; }
\n        rgb = mix(fog_rgb, rgb, factor);
\n    // Rain's forced fog: grey over the draw's own start/end, whatever the scene fog; grey is
\n    // neutral under Mod2x, so this is the streaks' distance fade.
\n    if (wow_params.fog.y > 0.5) {
\n        let denom = max(wow_params.fog.w - wow_params.fog.z, 0.001);
\n        let factor = clamp((wow_params.fog.w - in.view_z) / denom, 0.0, 1.0);
\n        rgb = mix(RAIN_FOG_GREY, rgb, factor);
\n#ifdef BLEND_ADD
\n    // Premultiplied in gamma, so stacked quads sum like the reference's bytes.
\n    return vec4<f32>(rgb * c.a, 0.0);
\n#else
\n#ifdef BLEND_OPAQUE
\n    return vec4<f32>(rgb, 1.0);
\n#else
\n#ifdef BLEND_ALPHAKEY
\n    // Blending is off (EGxBlend 1 → `glDisable(GL_BLEND)`); the surviving fragments are solid.
\n    return vec4<f32>(rgb, 1.0);
\n#else
\n#ifdef BLEND_MULTIPLY
\n    return vec4<f32>(rgb * c.a, c.a);
\n#else
\n#ifdef BLEND_MOD2X
\n    return vec4<f32>(rgb, 1.0);
\n#else
\n    return vec4<f32>(rgb, c.a);
\n#endif
\n#endif
\n#endif
\n#endif
\n#endif
\n#endif
shaders/static_gx.wgsl// The retained static-world pass: `wow_model.wgsl`'s shading for statics that never fade or
\n// animate (ADT doodads, WMO groups, interior M2 props), with per-vertex flag words and a per-item
\n// record in place of materials. `StaticGx::divert` admits opaque and alpha-tested batches with no
\n// env map and no depth flags. The light prefix, helpers and lighting lanes copy `wow_model.wgsl`'s
\n// and must stay in sync: naga_oil cannot import functions that use another module's bindings.
\n#import bevy_render::view::View
\n@group(0) @binding(0) var<uniform> view: View;
\n// Prefix of lighting::global_light's buffer; field order in sync with it and wow_model.wgsl.
\nstruct WowLight {
\n    light_ambient: vec4<f32>,
\n    light_diffuse: vec4<f32>,
\n    light_sun: vec4<f32>,
\n    light_spec: vec4<f32>,
\n    fog_color: vec4<f32>,
\n    fog_params: vec4<f32>,
\n    sh_c10_r: vec4<f32>,
\n    sh_c10_g: vec4<f32>,
\n    sh_c10_b: vec4<f32>,
\n    sh_c13_r: vec4<f32>,
\n    sh_c13_g: vec4<f32>,
\n    sh_c13_b: vec4<f32>,
\n    sh_c16: vec4<f32>,
\n    _water: array<vec4<f32>, 4>,
\n    grade: vec4<f32>,
\n    wmo_fog_color: vec4<f32>,
\n    wmo_fog_params: vec4<f32>,
\n    point_count: vec4<f32>,
\n    points: array<vec4<f32>, 512>,
\n    // lighting::prop_probes: 8192 slots of 7 rows; the buffer's later regions are not mirrored.
\n    prop_probes: array<vec4<f32>, 57344>,
\n@group(0) @binding(1) var<storage, read> wow_light: WowLight;
\n// Per-cell state (static_gx/render.rs `cell_layout`).
\nstruct GxCell {
\n    origin: vec4<f32>, // xyz = the bake's recentring origin
\n@group(1) @binding(0) var<uniform> cell: GxCell;
\n// The per-item records, indexed by the vertex word's low 16 bits: x the texture-array layer, y
\n// the WMO batch order (0 on cells), z the MOMT SIDN colour r|g<<8|b<<16 in gamma bytes, w flags:
\n// bit 0 exile kill, bits 1..=13 the interior-prop probe slot, bit 14 interior fog (`[0xca7f00]`).
\n@group(1) @binding(1) var<storage, read> recs: array<vec4<u32>>;
\n@group(1) @binding(2) var tex_array: texture_2d_array<f32>;
\n// Repeat and clamp model-albedo samplers: trilinear, aniso 8, the same as the entity path's.
\n@group(1) @binding(3) var samp_repeat: sampler;
\n@group(1) @binding(4) var samp_clamp: sampler;
\n// Vertex word bits; keep in sync with static_gx/mod.rs WORD_*.
\nconst WORD_WRAP_X: u32 = 65536u;    // 1 << 16
\nconst WORD_WRAP_Y: u32 = 131072u;   // 1 << 17
\nconst WORD_UNLIT: u32 = 262144u;    // 1 << 18
\nconst WORD_FOG_OFF: u32 = 524288u;  // 1 << 19
\nconst WORD_SHADE_LIT: u32 = 1048576u; // 1 << 20: ShadeSel::Lit, which no static carries
\nconst WORD_TEXTURED: u32 = 2097152u;  // 1 << 21
\n// The WMO lane: the entity path's per-material facts as bits.
\nconst WORD_WMO: u32 = 4194304u;        // 1 << 22: model_flags.x, a WMO surface
\nconst WORD_INTERIOR: u32 = 8388608u;   // 1 << 23: model_flags.z, an interior group
\nconst WORD_CLASS_INT: u32 = 16777216u; // 1 << 24: tint.w == 1, an INT batch
\nconst WORD_CLASS_TRANS: u32 = 33554432u; // 1 << 25: tint.w == 2, a TRANS batch
\nconst WORD_WINDOW: u32 = 67108864u;    // 1 << 26: sidn.w, the WINDOW midpoint light
\nconst WORD_HAS_VC: u32 = 134217728u;   // 1 << 27: the batch authors vertex colours
\n// INTERIOR without WMO is an interior M2 prop, the entity shader's `interior_prop =
\n// flags.z && !flags.x`: probe lighting, interior fog, no point lights.
\nconst WORD_MATTE: u32 = 268435456u;    // 1 << 28: ShadeSel::Matte, fixed intensity 1.0
\n// The alpha-test cutout reference 224/255, as wow_model.wgsl's VANILLA_ALPHA_KEY.
\nconst VANILLA_ALPHA_KEY: f32 = 0.8784314;
\n// ---- mirrored law (wow_model.wgsl) ----
\nfn wow_normalize(v: vec3<f32>) -> vec3<f32> {
\n    let l2 = dot(v, v);
\n    return select(vec3<f32>(0.0), normalize(v), l2 > 1e-12);
\nfn point_light_sum(P: vec3<f32>, N: vec3<f32>, anchor: vec3<f32>) -> vec3<f32> {
\n    let count = u32(wow_light.point_count.x);
\n    var sel = array<u32, 3>(0u, 0u, 0u);
\n    var sd = array<f32, 3>(1e30, 1e30, 1e30);
\n    for (var i = 0u; i < count; i = i + 1u) {
\n        let pos_range = wow_light.points[2u * i];
\n        let dv = pos_range.xyz - anchor;
\n        let d2 = dot(dv, dv);
\n        if (d2 > pos_range.w * pos_range.w) {
\n            continue;
\n            sd[2] = sd[1]; sel[2] = sel[1];
\n            sd[1] = sd[0]; sel[1] = sel[0];
\n            sd[0] = d2; sel[0] = i;
\n        } else if (d2 < sd[1]) {
\n            sd[2] = sd[1]; sel[2] = sel[1];
\n            sd[1] = d2; sel[1] = i;
\n        } else if (d2 < sd[2]) {
\n            sd[2] = d2; sel[2] = i;
\n    var sum = vec3<f32>(0.0);
\n    for (var s = 0u; s < 3u; s = s + 1u) {
\n            break;
\n        let pos_range = wow_light.points[2u * sel[s]];
\n        let to_light = pos_range.xyz - P;
\n        let d = length(to_light);
\n        let atten = 1.0 / (0.7 * d + 0.03 * d * d);
\n        let nl = max(dot(N, to_light / max(d, 1e-4)), 0.0);
\n        sum += wow_light.points[2u * sel[s] + 1u].rgb * (atten * nl);
\n    return sum;
\n// ---- the pass ----
\nstruct GxVertex {
\n    @location(0) position: vec3<f32>,
\n    @location(1) normal: vec3<f32>,
\n    @location(2) uv: vec2<f32>,
\n    @location(3) word: u32,
\n    @location(4) anchor: vec3<f32>,
\n    // MOCV or the baked constant tint; white where the batch authors none (WORD_HAS_VC).
\n    @location(5) color: vec4<f32>,
\nstruct GxVsOut {
\n    @builtin(position) position: vec4<f32>,
\n    @location(0) world_position: vec4<f32>,
\n    @location(1) world_normal: vec3<f32>,
\n    @location(2) uv: vec2<f32>,
\n    @location(3) @interpolate(flat) word: u32,
\n    @location(4) point_lit: vec3<f32>,
\n    @location(5) color: vec4<f32>,
\n@vertex
\nfn vertex(v: GxVertex) -> GxVsOut {
\n    var out: GxVsOut;
\n    // Exile kill bit (record w bit 0): every vertex of the item collapses to one point, so its
\n    // triangles are zero-area and rasterize nothing; triangles never span items.
\n    if ((recs[v.word & 0xffffu].w & 1u) != 0u) {
\n        out.position = vec4<f32>(0.0, 0.0, 2.0, 1.0);
\n        out.world_position = vec4<f32>(0.0);
\n        out.world_normal = vec3<f32>(0.0, 1.0, 0.0);
\n        out.uv = vec2<f32>(0.0);
\n        out.word = v.word;
\n        out.point_lit = vec3<f32>(0.0);
\n        out.color = vec4<f32>(1.0);
\n        return out;
\n    // Camera-relative for f32 precision: the recentred vertex plus (cell origin - camera).
\n    let p_cam = v.position + (cell.origin.xyz - view.world_position);
\n    let world = v.position + cell.origin.xyz;
\n    out.world_position = vec4<f32>(world, 1.0);
\n    let view_rot = mat3x3<f32>(
\n        view.view_from_world[0].xyz,
\n        view.view_from_world[1].xyz,
\n        view.view_from_world[2].xyz,
\n    out.position = view.clip_from_view * vec4<f32>(view_rot * p_cam, 1.0);
\n    // Authored MOBA batch order (record y, 0 on cells): a later coplanar batch wins reverse-Z
\n    // GreaterEqual in any draw order, because the draw sort does not keep authored order.
\n    out.position.z *= 1.0 + f32(recs[v.word & 0xffffu].y) * 1.1920929e-7;
\n    out.world_normal = v.normal;
\n    out.uv = v.uv;
\n    out.word = v.word;
\n    out.color = v.color;
\n    // Up to 3 nearest point lights, chosen from the placement origin. WMO surfaces take none,
\n    // as in the reference; interior props neither: the probe holds their group's MOLR lights.
\n    if ((v.word & (WORD_WMO | WORD_INTERIOR)) != 0u) {
\n        out.point_lit = vec3<f32>(0.0);
\n    } else {
\n        out.point_lit = point_light_sum(world, v.normal, v.anchor);
\n    return out;
\n@fragment
\nfn fragment(in: GxVsOut) -> @location(0) vec4<f32> {
\n    // The hard farclip wall: per-pixel planar eye-Z, the same plane as the entity path.
\n    let eye_z = -(view.view_from_world * vec4<f32>(in.world_position.xyz, 1.0)).z;
\n    if (wow_light.fog_params.w > 0.0 && eye_z > wow_light.fog_params.w) {
\n        discard;
\n    // The sampler follows the wrap flags; a mixed batch clamps its clamped axis a half texel in.
\n    // The derivatives are taken unconditionally (see below) and the select is per fragment.
\n    var base = vec4<f32>(1.0);
\n    let wrap_x = (in.word & WORD_WRAP_X) != 0u;
\n    let wrap_y = (in.word & WORD_WRAP_Y) != 0u;
\n    // The samples below sit inside a per-fragment branch (`WORD_TEXTURED` is per vertex), where
\n    // WGSL's uniformity rule forbids implicit derivatives — naga lets it through, the browser's
\n    // compiler does not. So the derivatives are taken HERE, in uniform flow, and the samples use
\n    // `textureSampleGrad`; `mip_bias` folds in as a scale of 2^bias on the footprint, which is
\n    // exactly what the bias form does to the LOD.
\n    let grad_scale = exp2(view.mip_bias);
\n    let uv_dx = dpdx(in.uv) * grad_scale;
\n    let uv_dy = dpdy(in.uv) * grad_scale;
\n    if ((in.word & WORD_TEXTURED) != 0u) {
\n        let layer = i32(recs[in.word & 0xffffu].x);
\n        let dims = vec2<f32>(textureDimensions(tex_array).xy);
\n        let inset = 0.5 / dims;
\n        var uv_mixed = in.uv;
\n        if (!wrap_x) {
\n            uv_mixed.x = clamp(uv_mixed.x, inset.x, 1.0 - inset.x);
\n        if (!wrap_y) {
\n            uv_mixed.y = clamp(uv_mixed.y, inset.y, 1.0 - inset.y);
\n        // The render-scale LOD bias: bevy's material path applies it for free, this lane by hand
\n        // (folded into the gradients above).
\n        let c_repeat = textureSampleGrad(tex_array, samp_repeat, in.uv, layer, uv_dx, uv_dy);
\n        let c_clamp = textureSampleGrad(tex_array, samp_clamp, in.uv, layer, uv_dx, uv_dy);
\n        let c_mixed = textureSampleGrad(tex_array, samp_repeat, uv_mixed, layer, uv_dx, uv_dy);
\n        if (wrap_x && wrap_y) {
\n            base = c_repeat;
\n        } else if (!wrap_x && !wrap_y) {
\n            base = c_clamp;
\n        } else {
\n            base = c_mixed;
\n#ifdef GX_CUTOUT
\n    if (base.a < VANILLA_ALPHA_KEY) {
\n        discard;
\n#endif
\n    // Both faces light from the submitted normal (no GL_LIGHT_MODEL_TWO_SIDE in the reference);
\n    // this pipeline never negates back faces, so it has no front-face select like wow_model.wgsl.
\n    let n_lit = wow_normalize(in.world_normal);
\n    let L = -normalize(wow_light.light_sun.xyz);
\n    let ndotl = max(dot(n_lit, L), 0.0);
\n    let lit_nl = clamp(
\n        wow_light.light_ambient.rgb + wow_light.light_diffuse.rgb * ndotl,
\n        vec3<f32>(0.0),
\n        vec3<f32>(1.0),
\n    // Order-2 SH basis terms of the fragment normal, for the doodad lobe and the probe lane.
\n    let quad = vec4<f32>(n_lit.x * n_lit.y, n_lit.y * n_lit.z, n_lit.z * n_lit.z, n_lit.x * n_lit.z);
\n    let x2y2 = n_lit.x * n_lit.x - n_lit.y * n_lit.y;
\n    // A colour-less batch takes a constant 1.0, not interpolated white: interpolating a constant
\n    // attribute gives 1.0±ε, and base × 0.99999994 rounds about half the pixels one byte down.
\n    let has_vc = (in.word & WORD_HAS_VC) != 0u;
\n    let vc = select(vec4<f32>(1.0), in.color, has_vc);
\n    let folded = select(base.rgb, base.rgb * vc.rgb, has_vc);
\n    var rgb: vec3<f32>;
\n    if ((in.word & WORD_WMO) != 0u) {
\n        // ---- WMO surfaces: wow_model.wgsl's is_wmo branch ----
\n        let interior = (in.word & WORD_INTERIOR) != 0u;
\n        let class_int = (in.word & WORD_CLASS_INT) != 0u;
\n        let class_trans = (in.word & WORD_CLASS_TRANS) != 0u;
\n        let trans_a = vc.a; // 1.0 where no MOCV is authored
\n        // WINDOW (MOMT 0x20), interior drawer only: GL_LIGHT0 becomes the Direct/Ambient
\n        // midpoint pair, ambient +16/255 saturating (0x6d37e0).
\n        let window_mid = 0.5 * (wow_light.light_ambient.rgb + wow_light.light_diffuse.rgb);
\n        let lit_window = clamp(
\n            window_mid + vec3<f32>(16.0 / 255.0) + window_mid * ndotl,
\n            vec3<f32>(0.0),
\n            vec3<f32>(1.0),
\n        let lit_int_base = select(lit_nl, lit_window, (in.word & WORD_WINDOW) != 0u);
\n        // Interior batch classes: INT is unlit (the bake is the room's light), TRANS lerps lit
\n        // to bake by MOCV alpha, EXT is plain lit_nl. Exterior groups take lit_nl at sun scale 1,
\n        // no terrain shade and no SH lobe (prog 198/VS 151).
\n        var lit_wmo_interior = vec3<f32>(1.0);
\n        if (class_trans) {
\n            lit_wmo_interior = mix(vec3<f32>(1.0), lit_int_base, trans_a);
\n        } else if (!class_int) {
\n            lit_wmo_interior = lit_int_base;
\n        let lit_wmo = select(lit_nl, lit_wmo_interior, interior);
\n        // SIDN night glow (MOMT 0x10): authored emissive × night fraction, an emission term
\n        // inside the clamp and never MOCV-multiplied; zero on INT, MOCV-alpha weighted on TRANS.
\n        let rec = recs[in.word & 0xffffu];
\n        let sidn_rgb = vec3<f32>(
\n            f32(rec.z & 0xffu),
\n            f32((rec.z >> 8u) & 0xffu),
\n            f32((rec.z >> 16u) & 0xffu),
\n        var sidn_w = 1.0;
\n        if (interior) {
\n            if (class_trans) {
\n                sidn_w = trans_a;
\n            } else if (class_int) {
\n                sidn_w = 0.0;
\n        let sidn_e = sidn_rgb * (wow_light.grade.x * sidn_w);
\n        // GL_COLOR_MATERIAL: MOCV multiplies the lit terms inside the clamp; emission adds beside.
\n        let primary = clamp(
\n            vc.rgb * (lit_wmo + in.point_lit) + sidn_e,
\n            vec3<f32>(0.0),
\n            vec3<f32>(1.0),
\n        // The entity path's algebra: (tex×vc)/max(vc, 1/255) is not tex in floats; keep it.
\n        let tex_rgb = folded / max(vc.rgb, vec3<f32>(1.0 / 255.0));
\n        rgb = tex_rgb * primary;
\n        if (interior && class_int && has_vc) {
\n            // INT self-illumination, the reference's interior pixel shader (literal 4.0):
\n            // tex·MOCV·(1 + 4·MOCV.a), clamped once. A colour-less INT batch keeps tex × lit.
\n            rgb = clamp(
\n                tex_rgb * vc.rgb * (1.0 + 4.0 * trans_a),
\n                vec3<f32>(0.0),
\n                vec3<f32>(1.0),
\n    } else if ((in.word & WORD_INTERIOR) != 0u) {
\n        // ---- interior M2 props: wow_model.wgsl's interior-prop branch ----
\n        // The spawn-folded SH probe (MODD ambient, fixed-axis diffuse, the group's MOLR lobes)
\n        // over the fragment normal; its soft wrap is the reference's, not a hard max(N·L, 0).
\n        let probe = 7u * ((recs[in.word & 0xffffu].w >> 1u) & 0x1fffu);
\n        let n1 = vec4<f32>(n_lit, 1.0);
\n        let lit_prop = clamp(
\n            vec3<f32>(
\n                dot(wow_light.prop_probes[probe + 0u], n1)
\n                    + dot(wow_light.prop_probes[probe + 3u], quad)
\n                    + wow_light.prop_probes[probe + 6u].x * x2y2,
\n                dot(wow_light.prop_probes[probe + 1u], n1)
\n                    + dot(wow_light.prop_probes[probe + 4u], quad)
\n                    + wow_light.prop_probes[probe + 6u].y * x2y2,
\n                dot(wow_light.prop_probes[probe + 2u], n1)
\n                    + dot(wow_light.prop_probes[probe + 5u], quad)
\n                    + wow_light.prop_probes[probe + 6u].z * x2y2,
\n            vec3<f32>(0.0),
\n            vec3<f32>(1.0),
\n        let primary = clamp(lit_prop + in.point_lit, vec3<f32>(0.0), vec3<f32>(1.0));
\n        rgb = folded * primary;
\n    } else {
\n        // ---- exterior ADT doodads and exterior MODD props ----
\n        // Model2.bls order-2 SH sun lobe at intensity 0.5 Shaded (MCSH), 1.0 Matte, 2.5 Lit.
\n        // Deviation: the `min(I, 1)` cap, as in wow_model.wgsl, since lifting it takes sun-facing
\n        // surfaces past 1.0; Matte keeps its own bit so it stays 1.0 if the cap goes.
\n        let shade_t = select(1.0, 0.0, (in.word & WORD_SHADE_LIT) != 0u);
\n        let intensity = min(
\n            select(mix(2.5, 0.5, shade_t), 1.0, (in.word & WORD_MATTE) != 0u),
\n        let sun_dc = wow_light.grade.yzw * intensity;
\n        let sun_lobe = vec3<f32>(
\n            wow_light.sh_c10_r.w + sun_dc.x
\n                + intensity
\n                    * (dot(wow_light.sh_c10_r.xyz, n_lit) + dot(wow_light.sh_c13_r, quad)
\n                        + wow_light.sh_c16.x * x2y2),
\n            wow_light.sh_c10_g.w + sun_dc.y
\n                + intensity
\n                    * (dot(wow_light.sh_c10_g.xyz, n_lit) + dot(wow_light.sh_c13_g, quad)
\n                        + wow_light.sh_c16.y * x2y2),
\n            wow_light.sh_c10_b.w + sun_dc.z
\n                + intensity
\n                    * (dot(wow_light.sh_c10_b.xyz, n_lit) + dot(wow_light.sh_c13_b, quad)
\n                        + wow_light.sh_c16.z * x2y2),
\n        let lit_doodad = clamp(sun_lobe, vec3<f32>(0.0), vec3<f32>(1.0));
\n        // Sun disabled (light_sun.w) falls back to the FFP matte, like the entity path.
\n        let lit = select(lit_nl, lit_doodad, wow_light.light_sun.w > 0.5);
\n        // FFP combine: the light sum saturates first, then the texture modulates it.
\n        let primary = clamp(lit + in.point_lit, vec3<f32>(0.0), vec3<f32>(1.0));
\n        rgb = folded * primary;
\n    // Unlit (M2 UNLIT 0x01, WMO UNLIT on an exterior group): texture × vertex colour, no light.
\n    if ((in.word & WORD_UNLIT) != 0u) {
\n        rgb = folded;
\n    // Planar eye-Z fog; other fog modes belong to blends never admitted here. The interior triple
\n    // keys on the per-frame record bit, not `WORD_INTERIOR`: the client sets it per group under
\n    // `[0xca7f00]` (`0x6b5190` for surfaces, `0x6b62e0` for the group's doodads).
\n    var fog_color = wow_light.fog_color;
\n    var fog_span = wow_light.fog_params.xy;
\n    if ((recs[in.word & 0xffffu].w & 16384u) != 0u) {
\n        fog_color = wow_light.wmo_fog_color;
\n        fog_span = wow_light.wmo_fog_params.xy;
\n    if (fog_color.w > 0.5 && (in.word & WORD_FOG_OFF) == 0u) {
\n        let denom = max(fog_span.y - fog_span.x, 0.001);
\n        let factor = clamp((fog_span.y - eye_z) / denom, 0.0, 1.0);
\n        rgb = mix(fog_color.xyz, rgb, factor);
\n    // Gamma-space output; alpha pinned 1.0, every draw here is opaque.
\n    return vec4<f32>(rgb, 1.0);
