\n//   diffuse  = clamp(ambient (row 1) + diffuse (row 0)·max(N·L, 0) + Σ point·att·N·L), evaluated
\n//     and clamped per vertex (GL T&L), Gouraud-interpolated, modulated 1× into the texture;
\n//   specular = clamp(row 9 · max(N·H, 0)^20) per vertex (local viewer), times the sheen mask (the
\n//     `_s` texture's per-texel alpha, blended like the colour), added after the modulate.
\n// Evaluated per pixel, or unmasked, the near-white row 9 would wash lit ground to cream.
\n// Bevy's `VertexOutput` has no slot for the interpolated specular, so the vertex transform and IO
\n// struct are our own and `main_pass_post_lighting_processing` is dropped; fog is in-shader.
\n#import bevy_pbr::{
\n    mesh_functions,
\n    forward_io::Vertex,
\n    view_transformations::position_world_to_clip,
\n    mesh_view_bindings::view,
\n@group(#{MATERIAL_BIND_GROUP}) @binding(100) var layer_array: texture_2d_array<f32>;
\n@group(#{MATERIAL_BIND_GROUP}) @binding(104) var alpha_array: texture_2d_array<f32>;
\n@group(#{MATERIAL_BIND_GROUP}) @binding(105) var splat_samp: sampler;
\n@group(#{MATERIAL_BIND_GROUP}) @binding(110) var shadow_array: texture_2d_array<f32>;
\n// Per-tile Vec4 uniforms, packed into one buffer (binding 106); the field order must match the Rust
\n// `TerrainExtension`. params.x = layer tiling factor; yzw unused.
\nstruct TerrainParams {
\n    params: vec4<f32>,
\n@group(#{MATERIAL_BIND_GROUP}) @binding(106) var<uniform> t: TerrainParams;
\n// The shared global light (`lighting::global_light`), updated in place once a frame; this mirrors
\n// its row layout, which must match.
\nstruct WowLight {
\n    light_ambient: vec4<f32>, // rgb = row 1 ambient; w = Mod2x scale (×1).
\n    light_diffuse: vec4<f32>, // rgb = row 0 sun diffuse; w = clamp-light flag (>0.5 ⇒ saturate).
\n    light_sun: vec4<f32>,     // xyz = world-space sun travel direction (to-light = −xyz); w unused.
\n    light_spec: vec4<f32>,    // rgb = row 9 specular color; w = shininess (20). rgb == 0 disables.
\n    fog_color: vec4<f32>,     // rgb = row 7 fog (raw, gamma 0..1); w = enable (>0.5 ⇒ blend).
\n    fog_params: vec4<f32>,    // x = fog_start yd; y = fog_end yd; z unused; w = farclip wall.
\n    _sh: array<vec4<f32>, 6>, // rows 6-11: model SH coefficients, unread by terrain.
\n    sh_c16: vec4<f32>,        // row 12: xyz = the models' c16 quad band; w free.
\n    _water: array<vec4<f32>, 4>, // rows 13-16: liquid swatches, unread by terrain.
\n    grade: vec4<f32>,         // row 17: reserved, layout only.
\n    _wmo_fog: array<vec4<f32>, 2>, // rows 18-19: interior fog, unread by terrain.
\n    // The dynamic point-light table (`global_light::build_light_data`): row 20 `.x` = live count,
\n    // then two rows per light, `[pos.xyz, range]` and `[rgb, 0]`.
\n    point_count: vec4<f32>,
\n    points: array<vec4<f32>, 512>,
\n@group(#{MATERIAL_BIND_GROUP}) @binding(90) var<storage, read> wow_light: WowLight;
\n// The vertex-to-fragment payload; `specular` is clamped per vertex, then Gouraud-interpolated.
\nstruct TerrainVsOut {
\n    @builtin(position) clip_position: vec4<f32>,
\n    @location(0) world_position: vec4<f32>,
\n    @location(2) uv: vec2<f32>,
\n    @location(3) uv_b: vec2<f32>,
\n    @location(4) color: vec4<f32>,
\n    @location(5) specular: vec3<f32>,
\n    // The Gouraud diffuse, summed and clamped per vertex as GL T&L does: an over-gamut light (a
\n    // carried torch is (1.4, 0.87, 0.40)) saturates one vertex and falls off linearly from it,
\n    // where clamping per pixel would pin a wide plateau at white.
\n    @location(6) primary: vec3<f32>,
\n// Terrain's point-light candidacy half-width (yd): `w + 10`, `w` being the chunk's bounding-sphere
\n// radius `sqrt(2·16.666666² + (zExtent/2)²)`, 23.570166 on flat ground (constant at `0x68dfac`).
\n// This takes the flat `w` everywhere, so steep chunks gather slightly narrower than the reference;
\n// the lights that differ are 33 yd out or more, where att ≈ 0.02.
\nconst TERRAIN_REACH: f32 = 33.570166;
\n// The dynamic point-light term. The reference commits at most three point lights per draw, the
\n// nearest by squared distance to the receiving unit, into GL slots 1-3; terrain's unit is the MCNK
\n// chunk, so `anchor` is its cell centre. Candidacy is a 20-yd spatial-hash sweep over
\n// `[floor((c - w - 10)/20), floor((c + w + 10)/20)]`, a Chebyshev box (`w` is `chunk+0x68`,
\n// copied at `0x71bc47`) of half-width `w + 10`, at least `TERRAIN_REACH`. A committed light is
\n// diffuse only (the ambient and specular slots are zeroed at `0x71c7e3`), falls off as
\n// `1/(0.7·d + 0.03·d²)` on the vertex normal, and has no distance cutoff. The M2 lane in
\n// wow_model.wgsl uses the packed per-light range: the lanes differ on purpose.
\nfn point_light_sum(P: vec3<f32>, N: vec3<f32>, anchor: vec3<f32>) -> vec3<f32> {
\n    let count = u32(wow_light.point_count.x);
\n    var sel = array<u32, 3>(0u, 0u, 0u);
\n    var sd = array<f32, 3>(1e30, 1e30, 1e30);
\n    for (var i = 0u; i < count; i = i + 1u) {
\n        let pos_range = wow_light.points[2u * i];
\n        let dv = pos_range.xyz - anchor;
\n        let d2 = dot(dv, dv);
\n        // The hash sweep is horizontal (the grid keys on WoW x/y = Bevy z/x) and has no vertical
\n        // bound; ranking below is the full 3-D distance, as `0x71bf90` does.
\n        if (max(abs(dv.x), abs(dv.z)) > TERRAIN_REACH) {
\n            continue;
\n            sd[2] = sd[1]; sel[2] = sel[1];
\n            sd[1] = sd[0]; sel[1] = sel[0];
\n            sd[0] = d2; sel[0] = i;
\n        } else if (d2 < sd[1]) {
\n            sd[2] = sd[1]; sel[2] = sel[1];
\n            sd[1] = d2; sel[1] = i;
\n        } else if (d2 < sd[2]) {
\n            sd[2] = d2; sel[2] = i;
\n    var sum = vec3<f32>(0.0);
\n    for (var s = 0u; s < 3u; s = s + 1u) {
\n            break;
\n        let pos_range = wow_light.points[2u * sel[s]];
\n        let to_light = pos_range.xyz - P;
\n        let d = length(to_light);
\n        let atten = 1.0 / (0.7 * d + 0.03 * d * d);
\n        let nl = max(dot(N, to_light / max(d, 1e-4)), 0.0);
\n        sum += wow_light.points[2u * sel[s] + 1u].rgb * (atten * nl);
\n    return sum;
\n// The MCNK chunk cell centre under a world point: the reference's light anchor, the chunk's world
\n// AABB centre `CMapChunk+0x5c..0x64` (written by `0x6b0e50`). The grid is fixed world-wide (chunk
\n// 533.33333/16 yd, half-extent 32 tiles) and symmetric, and WoW x/y are Bevy −z/−x, so snapping
\n// Bevy x/z lands on the same cells; wow_model.wgsl mirrors it for clutter.
\n// The anchor height is the vertex's own y, not the chunk's mid-height `(minH + maxH)/2`, so on
\n// relief one chunk's vertices can select different lights: the per-chunk constant is not plumbed
\n// to the vertex stage. On flat ground the two agree.
\nfn mcnk_cell_anchor(P: vec3<f32>) -> vec3<f32> {
\n    let cell = 533.33333 / 16.0;
\n    let half = 32.0 * 533.33333;
\n    let ix = floor((half + P.x) / cell);
\n    let iz = floor((half + P.z) / cell);
\n    return vec3<f32>((ix + 0.5) * cell - half, P.y, (iz + 0.5) * cell - half);
\n@vertex
\nfn vertex(in: Vertex) -> TerrainVsOut {
\n    var out: TerrainVsOut;
\n    let world_from_local = mesh_functions::get_world_from_local(in.instance_index);
\n    out.world_position =
\n        mesh_functions::mesh_position_local_to_world(world_from_local, vec4<f32>(in.position, 1.0));
\n    out.clip_position = position_world_to_clip(out.world_position.xyz);
\n    let world_normal = mesh_functions::mesh_normal_local_to_world(in.normal, in.instance_index);
\n    out.uv = in.uv;
\n    out.uv_b = in.uv_b;
\n    out.color = in.color;
\n    // Sun specular per vertex: white material, row-9 colour, shininess `light_spec.w` (20), local
\n    // viewer; clamped here, then Gouraud-interpolated.
\n    let n = normalize(world_normal);
\n    let l = -normalize(wow_light.light_sun.xyz); // to-light (the sun travels along +light_sun)
\n    let v = normalize(view.world_position.xyz - out.world_position.xyz); // to-eye (local viewer)
\n    let h = normalize(l + v);
\n    let ndoth = max(dot(n, h), 0.0);
\n    out.specular = clamp(wow_light.light_spec.rgb * pow(ndoth, wow_light.light_spec.w), vec3<f32>(0.0), vec3<f32>(1.0));
\n    // The whole diffuse sum on the MCNR normal, clamped per vertex: ambient, sun N·L, and the
\n    // chunk's three nearest point lights with their over-gamut colours raw.
\n    let ndotl = max(dot(n, l), 0.0);
\n    let points = point_light_sum(out.world_position.xyz, n, mcnk_cell_anchor(out.world_position.xyz));
\n    out.primary = clamp(
\n        wow_light.light_ambient.rgb + wow_light.light_diffuse.rgb * ndotl + points,
\n        vec3<f32>(0.0),
\n        vec3<f32>(1.0),
\n    return out;
\n@fragment
\nfn fragment(in: TerrainVsOut) -> @location(0) vec4<f32> {
\n    // The far-clip wall: the reference clips the detailed world per pixel at its far plane
\n    // (`farclip`, about 777 yd). Discard beyond `fog_params.w` (0 disables) on planar eye-Z.
\n    if (wow_light.fog_params.w > 0.0) {
\n        let clip_z = -(view.view_from_world * vec4<f32>(in.world_position.xyz, 1.0)).z;
\n        if (clip_z > wow_light.fog_params.w) {
\n            discard;
\n    // Per-chunk array indices baked per vertex, COLOR the 4 layers and UV1.x the alpha; constant
\n    // across a chunk, so they interpolate back to the integer.
\n    let li = vec4<i32>(round(in.color));
\n    let ai = i32(round(in.uv_b.x));
\n    let tiled = in.uv * t.params.x;
\n    // `.a` is the `_s` texture's sheen mask, 0 without an `_s`. `view.mip_bias` undoes the coarser
\n    // mip a render scale below 1 picks; the alpha and shadow arrays have one mip, so only the
\n    // layers take it.
\n    let s0 = textureSampleBias(layer_array, splat_samp, tiled, li.x, view.mip_bias);
\n    let s1 = textureSampleBias(layer_array, splat_samp, tiled, li.y, view.mip_bias);
\n    let s2 = textureSampleBias(layer_array, splat_samp, tiled, li.z, view.mip_bias);
\n    let s3 = textureSampleBias(layer_array, splat_samp, tiled, li.w, view.mip_bias);
\n    // The alpha and shadow maps (one untiled 64² grid per chunk) share the layers' repeat sampler,
\n    // so a linear footprint at a chunk edge would wrap to the far edge; a half-texel inset clamps.
\n    let auv = clamp(in.uv, vec2<f32>(0.5 / 64.0), vec2<f32>(1.0 - 0.5 / 64.0));
\n    let a = textureSample(alpha_array, splat_samp, auv, ai);
\n    var color = s0.rgb;
\n    color = mix(color, s1.rgb, a.r);
\n    color = mix(color, s2.rgb, a.g);
\n    color = mix(color, s3.rgb, a.b);
\n    // The sheen mask, blended with the colour's splat weights (the fragment program's
\n    // `secondary · texture[0].w`).
\n    var specmask = s0.a;
\n    specmask = mix(specmask, s1.a, a.r);
\n    specmask = mix(specmask, s2.a, a.g);
\n    specmask = mix(specmask, s3.a, a.b);
\n    let primary = in.primary;
\n    // MCSH baked shadow. With `pixelShaders` and `specular` on, terrain is one pass through
\n    // `terrainp_s.bls`, which reads the MCSH bit from the blend texture's alpha (1 lit, 0 shadowed)
\n    // and uses it twice, below; with them off the reference draws a separate ambient-tint overlay.
\n    // Our `shadow_array` is 255 shadowed, 0 lit; a chunk with no MCSH map (`uv_b.y < 0`) is lit.
\n    var shadow_lit = 1.0;
\n    let si = in.uv_b.y;
\n        // `textureSampleLevel`, not `textureSample`: this sits in a per-fragment branch, and WGSL's
\n        // uniformity rule (enforced by the browser's compiler, not by naga) forbids the implicit
\n        // derivative there. The shadow grid has one mip anyway, so level 0 is the same sample.
\n        let mcsh = textureSampleLevel(shadow_array, splat_samp, auv, i32(round(si)), 0.0).r;
\n        shadow_lit = 1.0 - mcsh;
\n    // The `terrainp_s.bls` combine, then an LDR clamp:
\n    //   diffuse  = tex · primary · (0.3·shadow + 0.7)   (a flat −30% in shadow, no tint)
\n    //   specular = sheen · mask · shadow                 (none in shadow)
\n    let diffuse_term = color * primary * (0.3 * shadow_lit + 0.7);
\n    let spec_term = in.specular * specmask * shadow_lit;
\n    var tuned = clamp(diffuse_term + spec_term, vec3<f32>(0.0), vec3<f32>(1.0));
\n    // Gamma-space GL_LINEAR fog on planar eye-Z, as the reference computes `fogcoord`, not radial
\n    // distance. Per pixel matches its per-vertex fog, since a linear factor interpolates exactly.
\n    if (wow_light.fog_color.w > 0.5) {
\n        let eye_z = -(view.view_from_world * vec4<f32>(in.world_position.xyz, 1.0)).z;
\n        let denom = max(wow_light.fog_params.y - wow_light.fog_params.x, 0.001);
\n        let factor = clamp((wow_light.fog_params.y - eye_z) / denom, 0.0, 1.0);
\n        tuned = mix(wow_light.fog_color.xyz, tuned, factor);
\n    // Raw gamma out: the framebuffer holds gamma bytes and blends in gamma like the reference's;
\n    // the frame's one decode is the FFXGlow combine.
\n    return vec4<f32>(tuned, 1.0);
shaders/wow_model.wgsl// The model pass for M2, WMO and ground-clutter meshes, lit and fogged in gamma space:
\n//   M2:           color = clamp01(A + D·I·(4/17)(0.375 + 2μ + 1.875μ²)) × tex × tint, μ = N·L
\n//   clutter, WMO: color = clamp(ambient + diffuse·max(N·L, 0)) × tex × tint
\n//   stage 1:      color = combine(color, tex1), tex1 at the generated coordinate (presets below)
\n//   fog:          color = mix(fog_color, color, fog_factor); out = color, raw gamma
\n// The M2 law is the order-2 SH lobe of `Shaders\Vertex\Model2.bls` (cvar `M2UseShaders`, default
\n// 1); M2's one FFP light site (`70bdf6`) runs only with that cvar off. Clutter and WMO are the FFP
\n// light (GL_LIGHTING, GL_LIGHT0, GL_COLOR_MATERIAL); clutter's normal is the terrain normal under
\n// the tuft, which the reference writes onto the clutter vertex.
\n// Not built: a specular term (the M2 per-material shininess is only inferred) and the WMO
\n// per-group authored colour.
\n#import bevy_pbr::{
\n    pbr_fragment::pbr_input_from_standard_material,
\n    pbr_functions::alpha_discard,
\n    pbr_bindings,
\n    forward_io::VertexOutput,
\n    mesh_view_bindings::view,
\n    mesh_functions,
\n// bevy_pbr 0.18.1's `forward_io::FragmentOutput`. No depth output: a fragment depth write costs
\n// the pipeline early-Z, so the sky lane pins its depth in the vertex stage.
\nstruct WowFragOut {
\n    @location(0) color: vec4<f32>,
\n// Per-material uniforms at binding 100, in `WowModelExt`'s field order (materials.rs).
\n//   clutter_fade: x = plateau-end view depth (yd, 0.75·far), y = ramp-zero view depth (the ~70 yd
\n//     detail-doodad horizon `[0x867958]`), z = the batch marker bits, w = clutter
\n//   model_flags: x = WMO, y = fade blend twin, z = interior (a WMO interior group, or an interior
\n//     M2 lit by its SH probe), w = unlit fullbright (M2 UNLIT 0x01 or Mod/Mod2x, or WMO UNLIT on
\n//     an exterior-group batch; the interior drawer ignores it)
\nstruct ModelParams {
\n    clutter_fade: vec4<f32>,
\n    model_flags: vec4<f32>,
\n    // x = the terrain-shade selector (see the doodad sun), y = the WMO batch order, zw = the
\n    // UV-scroll seed.
\n    sun_scale: vec4<f32>,
\n    // xyz = the animated M2Color tint (identity when static); w = the WMO interior batch class:
\n    // 0 exterior law, 1 INT, 2 TRANS.
\n    tint: vec4<f32>,
\n    // WMO glass, 0 on M2: xyz = the MOMT SIDN (0x10) emissive (gamma /255), w = MOMT WINDOW (0x20).
\n    sidn: vec4<f32>,
\n    // Rows of `wow_light.matanim`, 0 = identity: x = UV scroll, y = tint, z = texture-transform
\n    // affine, w = the UI tile's cell clip.
\n    anim_slots: vec4<f32>,
\n    // The second texture stage: x = bound (1) or not (0), y = its combine preset 0-5; zw unused.
\n    stage1: vec4<f32>,
\n@group(#{MATERIAL_BIND_GROUP}) @binding(100) var<uniform> m: ModelParams;
\n// Stage 1's texture, sampled at the generated coordinate `env_uv` when `m.stage1.x` is set.
\n@group(#{MATERIAL_BIND_GROUP}) @binding(101) var stage1_texture: texture_2d<f32>;
\n@group(#{MATERIAL_BIND_GROUP}) @binding(102) var stage1_sampler: sampler;
\n// The shared light buffer (`lighting::global_light`, rows as packed there), updated once per
\n// frame; terrain.wgsl mirrors the prefix, so a tree and the ground under it fog alike.
\nstruct WowLight {
\n    light_ambient: vec4<f32>, // rgb ambient; w = Mod2x scale
\n    light_diffuse: vec4<f32>, // rgb sun diffuse; w = clamp-light flag (>0.5 ⇒ saturate)
\n    light_sun: vec4<f32>,     // xyz sun travel dir (to-light = −xyz); w = directional enable
\n    light_spec: vec4<f32>,    // terrain's specular (w = its shininess); unread here
\n    fog_color: vec4<f32>,     // rgb row-7 fog (gamma); w = enable (>0.5)
\n    fog_params: vec4<f32>,    // x = start, y = end, w = farclip wall; z unused
\n    // Rows 6-12: the reference's `Model2.bls` order-2 SH probe of the scene light at intensity 1:
\n    // ambient DC in the c10 `.w` lanes, the sun's bands in c10.xyz, c13 and c16.xyz. Every sun band
\n    // is linear in the committed colour, so all scale by the intensity (never I²).
\n    sh_c10_r: vec4<f32>,
\n    sh_c10_g: vec4<f32>,
\n    sh_c10_b: vec4<f32>,
\n    sh_c13_r: vec4<f32>,
\n    sh_c13_g: vec4<f32>,
\n    sh_c13_b: vec4<f32>,
\n    // xyz = the c16 quadratic band (x²−y²) per channel; w unused.
\n    sh_c16: vec4<f32>,
\n    _water: array<vec4<f32>, 4>, // rows 13-16: the liquid swatches, unread here
\n    // x = the SIDN night fraction (1 overnight, 0 by day); yzw = the sun's SH DC at intensity 1.
\n    grade: vec4<f32>,
\n    // Rows 18-19: the interior fog, the 4 s camera-in-WMO MFOG crossfade (the scene fog outdoors).
\n    wmo_fog_color: vec4<f32>,    // rgb interior fog (gamma); w = enable (mirrors fog_color.w)
\n    wmo_fog_params: vec4<f32>,   // x = start yd, y = end yd; zw unused
\n    // Row 20 `.x` = the point-light count, then per light `[pos.xyz, range]`, `[rgb, 0]`. Here, not
\n    // in Bevy's clusterables, which the view layout gives the fragment stage only.
\n    point_count: vec4<f32>,
\n    points: array<vec4<f32>, 512>,
\n    // The interior-prop SH probes, 7 rows per slot (`MAX_PROP_PROBES` = 8192 slots). Only this
\n    // shader declares this tail; the other shaders bind the same buffer by its prefix.
\n    prop_probes: array<vec4<f32>, 57344>,
\n    // Per rig slot (sizes mirrored in rig_palette.rs): the base bone index into `palettes`, whose
\n    // 3 rows per bone are `rig_from_joint × inverse_bindpose` from the rig's own origin.
\n    rig_table: array<u32, 2048>,
\n    // Per rig slot: the CM2 body tint (`model+0x184/188/18c`) packed `0xFFRRGGBB` like the
\n    // reference's node value (`0x60d840`: `param | 0xff000000`); 0 is identity.
\n    rig_tint: array<u32, 2048>,
\n    // Per rig slot: the world origin its palette rows are measured from.
\n    rig_origin: array<vec4<f32>, 2048>,
\n    // The mat-anim rows (size mirrored in mat_anim_table.rs), row 0 zero: a UV-scroll delta (xy),
\n    // a tint delta (xyz), a texture-transform affine `[cos − 1, sin, sx − 1, sy − 1]` or a UI cell.
\n    matanim: array<vec4<f32>, 2048>,
\n    // Per rig slot, the straddle waterline (size mirrored in straddle.rs): x = its world height
\n    // (Bevy Y), y = the side the near copy keeps (+1 above, −1 below, 0 not straddling).
\n    water_clip: array<vec2<f32>, 2048>,
\n    palettes: array<vec4<f32>>,
\n@group(#{MATERIAL_BIND_GROUP}) @binding(90) var<storage, read> wow_light: WowLight;
\n// The M2 cutout alpha-test reference, 224/255; in sync with `materials::VANILLA_ALPHA_KEY_REF`.
\nconst VANILLA_ALPHA_KEY: f32 = 0.8784314;
\n// The detail-doodad pass's stage-0 `D3DSAMP_MIPMAPLODBIAS = +0.25` (`0x6813f4`).
\nconst DETAIL_DOODAD_LOD_BIAS: f32 = 0.25;
\n// Bevy's `VertexOutput` (same fields, locations and defs; no tangents, morphs or visibility
\n// ranges) plus our interpolants; the fragment rebuilds a `VertexOutput` from it.
\nstruct WowVsOut {
\n    @builtin(position) position: vec4<f32>,
\n    @location(0) world_position: vec4<f32>,
\n    @location(1) world_normal: vec3<f32>,
\n#ifdef VERTEX_UVS_A
\n    @location(2) uv: vec2<f32>,
\n#endif
\n#ifdef VERTEX_UVS_B
\n    @location(3) uv_b: vec2<f32>,
\n#endif
\n#ifdef VERTEX_COLORS
\n    @location(5) color: vec4<f32>,
\n#endif
\n#ifdef VERTEX_OUTPUT_INSTANCE_INDEX
\n    @location(6) @interpolate(flat) instance_index: u32,
\n#endif
\n    // The point-light sum `Σ att·sat(N·L)·colour`, per vertex like the reference FFP.
\n    @location(8) point_lit: vec3<f32>,
\n#ifdef WOW_MERGED_FADE
\n    // A merged blob's per-placement fade alpha, constant over the placement.
\n    @location(9) merged_fade: f32,
\n#endif
\n#ifdef WOW_MERGED_SLOT
\n    @location(10) @interpolate(flat) merged_slot: u32,
\n#endif
\n    // Stage 1's generated coordinate, (0, 0) when the material binds no stage 1.
\n    @location(11) env_uv: vec2<f32>,
\n// The generated environment coordinate of `Model2.bls` (its programs for a stage whose coordinate
\n// lookup is above 2, `0x70b8bd`): in view space R = normalize(P − 2(P·N)N), uv = R.xy·0.5 + 0.5,
\n// per vertex. The reference view basis (`0x5c3e70`) and Bevy's −Z-forward one differ only in z,
\n// so R.xy needs no fixup.
\nfn wow_env_uv(p_view: vec3<f32>, n_view: vec3<f32>) -> vec2<f32> {
\n    let refl = normalize(p_view - 2.0 * dot(p_view, n_view) * n_view);
\n    return refl.xy * 0.5 + vec2<f32>(0.5, 0.5);
\n// Stage 1's colour combine on `prev`, the stage-0 result, by gx preset as the default device,
\n// Direct3D, maps it (`0x80a25c` = 4, 4, 13, 7, 5, 12 as `D3DTOP`, args TEXTURE and CURRENT, which
\n// the device never changes): 0 and 1 modulate, 2 BLENDTEXTUREALPHA interpolates by the texel's
\n// alpha, 3 adds, 4 modulates ×2, 5 BLENDDIFFUSEALPHA interpolates by `diffuse_a`, the vertex
\n// colour's alpha. Each stage's result saturates.
\nfn stage1_rgb(preset: u32, prev: vec3<f32>, tex: vec4<f32>, diffuse_a: f32) -> vec3<f32> {
\n    var c = prev * tex.rgb;
\n    if (preset == 2u) {
\n        c = mix(prev, tex.rgb, tex.a);
\n    } else if (preset == 3u) {
\n        c = prev + tex.rgb;
\n    } else if (preset == 4u) {
\n        c = 2.0 * prev * tex.rgb;
\n    } else if (preset == 5u) {
\n        c = mix(prev, tex.rgb, diffuse_a);
\n    return clamp(c, vec3<f32>(0.0), vec3<f32>(1.0));
\n// A stage's alpha on `prev`, the previous stage's (the diffuse alpha, for stage 0), by gx preset
\n// (`0x80a274`, args TEXTURE and CURRENT): 1 modulates, 3 adds, 4 modulates ×2, the rest
\n// (SELECTARG2) pass the previous.
\nfn stage_alpha(preset: u32, prev: f32, tex: f32) -> f32 {
\n    var a = prev;
\n    if (preset == 1u) {
\n        a = prev * tex;
\n    } else if (preset == 3u) {
\n        a = prev + tex;
\n    } else if (preset == 4u) {
\n        a = 2.0 * prev * tex;
\n    return clamp(a, 0.0, 1.0);
\n// Zero-safe normalize. M2s author `(0,0,0)` normals (`Creature\QuirajProphet`) and the reference
\n// lights them: `Model2.bls` normalizes with `RSQ`/`MUL`, where `0 × INF` is 0, leaving the SH DC
\n// term. `normalize(0)` is NaN, which clamps to 0 and blacks the batch. Wrapping `normalize`
\n// rather than `v · inverseSqrt(l2)` keeps every nonzero normal's bits.
\nfn wow_normalize(v: vec3<f32>) -> vec3<f32> {
\n    let l2 = dot(v, v);
\n    return select(vec3<f32>(0.0), normalize(v), l2 > 1e-12);
\n// The point lights at P: the reference commits at most three per draw, the nearest to the
\n// receiving unit's own position `anchor` (`0x71bf90` gathers by squared distance, `0x71c730` seats
\n// slots 1-3). Range bounds candidacy only; a selected light falls off as `1/(0.7·d + 0.03·d²)`,
\n// diffuse only, on the submitted normal (no GL_LIGHT_MODEL_TWO_SIDE). Mirrored in terrain.wgsl.
\nfn point_light_sum(P: vec3<f32>, N: vec3<f32>, anchor: vec3<f32>) -> vec3<f32> {
\n    let count = u32(wow_light.point_count.x);
\n    var sel = array<u32, 3>(0u, 0u, 0u);
\n    var sd = array<f32, 3>(1e30, 1e30, 1e30);
\n    for (var i = 0u; i < count; i = i + 1u) {
\n        let pos_range = wow_light.points[2u * i];
\n        let dv = pos_range.xyz - anchor;
\n        let d2 = dot(dv, dv);
\n        if (d2 > pos_range.w * pos_range.w) {
\n            continue;
\n            sd[2] = sd[1]; sel[2] = sel[1];
\n            sd[1] = sd[0]; sel[1] = sel[0];
\n            sd[0] = d2; sel[0] = i;
\n        } else if (d2 < sd[1]) {
\n            sd[2] = sd[1]; sel[2] = sel[1];
\n            sd[1] = d2; sel[1] = i;
\n        } else if (d2 < sd[2]) {
\n            sd[2] = d2; sel[2] = i;
\n    var sum = vec3<f32>(0.0);
\n    for (var s = 0u; s < 3u; s = s + 1u) {
\n            break;
\n        let pos_range = wow_light.points[2u * sel[s]];
\n        let to_light = pos_range.xyz - P;
\n        let d = length(to_light);
\n        let atten = 1.0 / (0.7 * d + 0.03 * d * d);
\n        let nl = max(dot(N, to_light / max(d, 1e-4)), 0.0);
\n        sum += wow_light.points[2u * sel[s] + 1u].rgb * (atten * nl);
\n    return sum;
\n// The centre of the MCNK chunk under P, the light anchor for world-merged clutter, since the
\n// reference gathers lights per terrain chunk (mirrored in terrain.wgsl). WoW x/y are Bevy −z/−x
\n// and the grid is symmetric, so snapping Bevy x/z lands on the same cells. The height is the
\n// vertex's own, not the chunk record's: lights sit near the surface.
\nfn mcnk_cell_anchor(P: vec3<f32>) -> vec3<f32> {
\n    let cell = 533.33333 / 16.0;
\n    let half = 32.0 * 533.33333;
\n    let ix = floor((half + P.x) / cell);
\n    let iz = floor((half + P.z) / cell);
\n    return vec3<f32>((ix + 0.5) * cell - half, P.y, (iz + 0.5) * cell - half);
\n#ifdef WOW_MERGED_FADE
\n// The doodad fade curve (`0x683f80`, in sync with `model_fade::doodad_fade_alpha`): alpha =
\n// 1 − (d − start)/range, d = horizontal distance − radius, over a size-bucketed band.
\nfn merged_fade_alpha(radius: f32, horiz_dist: f32) -> f32 {
\n    if (radius > 7.0) {
\n        return 1.0;
\n    var start = 150.0;
\n    var range = 50.0;
\n    if (radius <= 0.5) {
\n        start = 40.0;
\n        range = 10.0;
\n    } else if (radius <= 2.5) {
\n        start = 100.0;
\n        range = 25.0;
\n    let d = horiz_dist - radius;
\n    return clamp(1.0 - (d - start) / range, 0.0, 1.0);
\n#endif
\n// Bevy 0.18's `forward_io::Vertex` at Bevy's locations, plus the palette joints at 10/11 (appended
\n// by `WowModelExt::specialize` for a mesh with `ATTRIBUTE_WOW_JOINT_INDEX`) and the merged-blob
\n// attributes at 12/13.
\nstruct WowVertex {
\n    @builtin(instance_index) instance_index: u32,
\n#ifdef VERTEX_POSITIONS
\n    @location(0) position: vec3<f32>,
\n#endif
\n#ifdef VERTEX_NORMALS
\n    @location(1) normal: vec3<f32>,
\n#endif
\n#ifdef VERTEX_UVS_A
\n    @location(2) uv: vec2<f32>,
\n#endif
\n#ifdef VERTEX_UVS_B
\n    @location(3) uv_b: vec2<f32>,
\n#endif
\n#ifdef VERTEX_COLORS
\n    @location(5) color: vec4<f32>,
\n#endif
\n#ifdef WOW_RIG_SKIN
\n    @location(10) joint_indices: vec4<u32>,
\n    @location(11) joint_weights: vec4<f32>,
\n#endif
\n#ifdef WOW_MERGED_FADE
\n    // The placement fade sphere: xyz = world centre, w = fade radius.
\n    @location(12) fade_sphere: vec4<f32>,
\n#endif
\n#ifdef WOW_MERGED_SLOT
\n    // The interior-prop SH-probe slot, in place of the per-entity MeshTag payload.
\n    @location(13) merged_slot: u32,
\n#endif
\n#ifdef WOW_RIG_SKIN
\nfn wow_rig_slot(instance_index: u32) -> u32 {
\n    return (mesh_functions::get_tag(instance_index) >> 19u) & 0x7ffu;
\n// Blends the four weighted bones' palette rows into `rig_from_local`, which replaces the mesh's
\n// world matrix like Bevy's `skin_model`; its translation is relative to `rig_origin[slot]`.
\nfn wow_skin_model(instance_index: u32, indices: vec4<u32>, weights: vec4<f32>) -> mat4x4<f32> {
\n    let base = wow_light.rig_table[wow_rig_slot(instance_index)];
\n    let b0 = 3u * (base + indices.x);
\n    let b1 = 3u * (base + indices.y);
\n    let b2 = 3u * (base + indices.z);
\n    let b3 = 3u * (base + indices.w);
\n    let r0 = weights.x * wow_light.palettes[b0]
\n        + weights.y * wow_light.palettes[b1]
\n        + weights.z * wow_light.palettes[b2]
\n        + weights.w * wow_light.palettes[b3];
\n    let r1 = weights.x * wow_light.palettes[b0 + 1u]
\n        + weights.y * wow_light.palettes[b1 + 1u]
\n        + weights.z * wow_light.palettes[b2 + 1u]
\n        + weights.w * wow_light.palettes[b3 + 1u];
\n    let r2 = weights.x * wow_light.palettes[b0 + 2u]
\n        + weights.y * wow_light.palettes[b1 + 2u]
\n        + weights.z * wow_light.palettes[b2 + 2u]
\n        + weights.w * wow_light.palettes[b3 + 2u];
\n    // r0/r1/r2 are the affine's rows; a WGSL matrix is column-major.
\n    return mat4x4<f32>(
\n        vec4<f32>(r0.x, r1.x, r2.x, 0.0),
\n        vec4<f32>(r0.y, r1.y, r2.y, 0.0),
\n        vec4<f32>(r0.z, r1.z, r2.z, 0.0),
\n        vec4<f32>(r0.w, r1.w, r2.w, 1.0),
\n// bevy_pbr::skinning's inverse-transpose via the adjugate, verbatim.
\nfn inverse_transpose_3x3m(in: mat3x3<f32>) -> mat3x3<f32> {
\n    let x = cross(in[1], in[2]);
\n    let y = cross(in[2], in[0]);
\n    let z = cross(in[0], in[1]);
\n    let det = dot(in[2], z);
\n    return mat3x3<f32>(x / det, y / det, z / det);
\nfn wow_skin_normals(frame_from_local: mat4x4<f32>, normal: vec3<f32>) -> vec3<f32> {
\n    return wow_normalize(
\n        inverse_transpose_3x3m(mat3x3<f32>(
\n            frame_from_local[0].xyz,
\n            frame_from_local[1].xyz,
\n            frame_from_local[2].xyz
\n        )) * normal
\n#endif
\n// Bevy 0.18's `mesh.wgsl` vertex stage plus our skinning and point lights. A `MaterialExtension`
\n// replaces the whole stage, so this must track Bevy's on upgrades.
\n@vertex
\nfn vertex(vertex: WowVertex) -> WowVsOut {
\n    var out: WowVsOut;
\n    let mesh_world_from_local = mesh_functions::get_world_from_local(vertex.instance_index);
\n    // Precision: `frame_from_local` holds the orientation and a small translation, `frame_origin`
\n    // the ~9 k yd world position, so no f32 product mixes the two (an f32 ULP at 9 k is ~1 mm).
\n#ifdef WOW_RIG_SKIN
\n    var frame_from_local = wow_skin_model(
\n        vertex.instance_index,
\n        vertex.joint_indices,
\n        vertex.joint_weights
\n    let frame_origin = wow_light.rig_origin[wow_rig_slot(vertex.instance_index)].xyz;
\n#else
\n    var frame_from_local = mesh_world_from_local;
\n    let frame_origin = mesh_world_from_local[3].xyz;
\n    frame_from_local[3] = vec4<f32>(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0);
\n#endif
\n#ifdef VERTEX_NORMALS
\n#ifdef WOW_RIG_SKIN
\n    out.world_normal = wow_skin_normals(frame_from_local, vertex.normal);
\n#else
\n    out.world_normal = mesh_functions::mesh_normal_local_to_world(
\n        vertex.normal,
\n        vertex.instance_index
\n#endif
\n#endif
\n#ifdef VERTEX_POSITIONS
\n    // Precision: camera-relative to clip space; `clip_from_world × p_world` cancels
\n    // catastrophically with camera and geometry near 9 k yd. `world_position` is absolute again:
\n    // lighting and fog need no such precision.
\n    let p_cam = (frame_from_local * vec4<f32>(vertex.position, 1.0)).xyz
\n        + (frame_origin - view.world_position);
\n    out.world_position = vec4<f32>(p_cam + view.world_position, 1.0);
\n    let view_rot = mat3x3<f32>(
\n        view.view_from_world[0].xyz,
\n        view.view_from_world[1].xyz,
\n        view.view_from_world[2].xyz,
\n    out.position = view.clip_from_view * vec4<f32>(view_rot * p_cam, 1.0);
\n    // WMO batch order (`sun_scale.y`, 0 off WMO): the reference layers coplanar batches by MOBA
\n    // draw order under depth-write + LEQUAL; Bevy reorders draws, so a later batch must win the
\n    // reverse-Z GreaterEqual test. Scaling clip z by (1 + n·2⁻²³) raises z/w by n ULPs. Uniform
\n    // data, not a `DepthBiasState`, which would make every batch index its own pipeline.
\n    out.position.z *= 1.0 + m.sun_scale.y * 1.1920929e-7;
\n#ifdef WOW_SKY_DEPTH
\n    // The WMO-skybox lane (`clutter_fade.z` bit 13): clip z = 0 is reverse-Z infinitely far, so
\n    // the world always draws over the sky shell (`benilla_world::sky_order`).
\n    out.position.z = 0.0;
\n#endif
\n#ifdef WOW_MERGED_FADE
\n    // A fully faded placement leaves the clip volume, so its triangles never rasterize.
\n    let fade_d = distance(view.world_position.xz, vertex.fade_sphere.xz);
\n    out.merged_fade = merged_fade_alpha(vertex.fade_sphere.w, fade_d);
\n    if (out.merged_fade <= 0.0) {
\n        out.position = vec4<f32>(0.0, 0.0, 2.0, 1.0);
\n#ifdef WOW_MERGED_SLOT
\n    out.merged_slot = vertex.merged_slot;
\n#endif
\n#endif
\n#endif
\n#ifdef VERTEX_UVS_A
\n    out.uv = vertex.uv;
\n    // Env-mapped batches (`clutter_fade.z` bit 12; `texture_unit_lookup[texCoordSet] > 2` at
\n    // `0x70b8bd`) generate their texcoord per vertex (`wow_env_uv`).
\n#ifdef VERTEX_POSITIONS
\n#ifdef VERTEX_NORMALS
\n    if ((u32(m.clutter_fade.z) & 4096u) != 0u) {
\n        out.uv = wow_env_uv(view_rot * p_cam, normalize(view_rot * out.world_normal));
\n#endif
\n#endif
\n#endif
\n    // Stage 1 takes the same generated coordinate in its own interpolant: a two-texture unit's
\n    // second lookup is the environment one in every stock model (`0xffff`).
\n    out.env_uv = vec2<f32>(0.0);
\n#ifdef VERTEX_POSITIONS
\n#ifdef VERTEX_NORMALS
\n    if (m.stage1.x > 0.5) {
\n        out.env_uv = wow_env_uv(view_rot * p_cam, normalize(view_rot * out.world_normal));
\n#endif
\n#endif
\n#ifdef VERTEX_UVS_B
\n    out.uv_b = vertex.uv_b;
\n#endif
\n#ifdef VERTEX_COLORS
\n    out.color = vertex.color;
\n#endif
\n#ifdef VERTEX_OUTPUT_INSTANCE_INDEX
\n    out.instance_index = vertex.instance_index;
\n#endif
\n    // Point lights: none on WMO surfaces, none here on interior M2 props (their group's MOLR lights
\n    // are in the SH probe), else the ≤3 nearest to the instance origin (clutter: its MCNK chunk).
\n    if (m.model_flags.x > 0.5 || m.model_flags.z > 0.5) {
\n        out.point_lit = vec3<f32>(0.0);
\n    } else {
\n        var anchor = mesh_world_from_local[3].xyz;
\n        if (m.clutter_fade.w > 0.5) {
\n            anchor = mcnk_cell_anchor(out.world_position.xyz);
\n        out.point_lit = point_light_sum(out.world_position.xyz, out.world_normal, anchor);
\n    return out;
\n@fragment
\nfn fragment(in: WowVsOut, @builtin(front_facing) is_front: bool) -> WowFragOut {
\n    // The clips below are decided here and discarded only after the texture samples: naga lowers
\n    // `discard` to SPIR-V OpKill, which ends a quad's helper lanes, and Intel's Vulkan drivers then
\n    // take implicit derivatives along every triangle edge from the dead lanes (the smallest mip in
\n    // dotted lines over the model). Tint defers its discards the same way.
\n    var clipped = false;
\n    // The UI model tile's cell clip: the reference gives each `<Model>` pane its widget rect as the
\n    // viewport; our panes share an atlas, so the tile passes its cell as a mat-anim row
\n    // (`anim_slots.w`, `[min.x, min.y, max.x, max.y]` in atlas texels) and this is the scissor.
\n    if (m.anim_slots.w > 0.5) {
\n        let r = wow_light.matanim[u32(m.anim_slots.w)];
\n        if (in.position.x < r.x || in.position.y < r.y
\n            || in.position.x > r.z || in.position.y > r.w) {
\n            clipped = true;
\n    // The far-clip wall: discard past `farclip` (`fog_params.w`, 0 = off) by planar eye depth, as
\n    // terrain.wgsl does.
\n    if (wow_light.fog_params.w > 0.0) {
\n        let clip_z = -(view.view_from_world * vec4<f32>(in.world_position.xyz, 1.0)).z;
\n        if (clip_z > wow_light.fog_params.w) {
\n            clipped = true;
\n#ifdef WOW_WATER_CLIP
\n    // The straddle split: a translucent model crossing its water plane draws on each side of the
\n    // water pass (the far copy has `clutter_fade.z` bit 11) and each copy keeps its half, the
\n    // reference's `M2UseClipPlanes` plane at the waterline. In sync with `straddle::keeps`.
\n    let water_clip = wow_light.water_clip[(mesh_functions::get_tag(in.instance_index) >> 19u) & 0x7ffu];
\n    if (water_clip.y != 0.0) {
\n        let far_copy = (u32(m.clutter_fade.z) & 2048u) != 0u;
\n        let keep_side = select(water_clip.y, -water_clip.y, far_copy);
\n        if (keep_side * (in.world_position.y - water_clip.x) < 0.0) {
\n            clipped = true;
\n#endif
\n    // Rebuild Bevy's `VertexOutput` with the M2 texture transform (in sync with
\n    // `tex_anim::uv_transform`): uv' = R((uv + t − p) ⊙ s) + p, p = (½, ½), t = `sun_scale.zw`
\n    // plus its mat-anim delta, R and s from the affine row `[cos − 1, sin, sx − 1, sy − 1]`.
\n    var vo: VertexOutput;
\n    vo.position = in.position;
\n    vo.world_position = in.world_position;
\n    vo.world_normal = in.world_normal;
\n#ifdef VERTEX_UVS_A
\n    // An env-mapped coordinate takes no UV animation: the reference excludes an env stage from
\n    // `textureTransform`.
\n    if ((u32(m.clutter_fade.z) & 4096u) != 0u) {
\n    } else {
\n        let uv_t = in.uv + m.sun_scale.zw + wow_light.matanim[u32(m.anim_slots.x)].xy;
\n        let affine = wow_light.matanim[u32(m.anim_slots.z)];
\n        let d = (uv_t - vec2<f32>(0.5, 0.5)) * vec2<f32>(1.0 + affine.z, 1.0 + affine.w);
\n        let c = 1.0 + affine.x;
\n        vo.uv = vec2<f32>(0.5 + d.x * c - d.y * affine.y, 0.5 + d.x * affine.y + d.y * c);
\n#endif
\n#ifdef VERTEX_UVS_B
\n#endif
\n#ifdef VERTEX_COLORS
\n    vo.color = in.color;
\n#endif
\n#ifdef VERTEX_OUTPUT_INSTANCE_INDEX
\n    vo.instance_index = in.instance_index;
\n#endif
\n    var pbr_input = pbr_input_from_standard_material(vo, is_front);
\n    var base_color = pbr_input.material.base_color;
\n    // WMO MOCV alpha is lighting data (the TRANS lerp, the INT glow mask), and the reference's WMO
\n    // output alpha is tex.a alone. Bevy folds the vertex alpha into base_color, so re-sample the
\n    // texel alpha: dividing the fold back out loses everything where MOCV.a ≈ 0.
\n#ifdef VERTEX_COLORS
\n    if (m.model_flags.x > 0.5) {
\n#ifdef VERTEX_UVS_A
\n        base_color.a = textureSampleBias(
\n            pbr_bindings::base_color_texture,
\n            pbr_bindings::base_color_sampler,
\n            // The colour's LOD: `pbr_input_from_standard_material` applies `view.mip_bias`, and
\n            // coverage from another mip erodes out of step with the art.
\n            view.mip_bias,
\n#else
\n        base_color.a = 1.0;
\n#endif
\n#endif
\n    // The detail-doodad LOD bias (`0x6813f4`): on the atlases whose alpha pyramid is binary below
\n    // mip 0 it keeps every fragment below full alpha, so the fade erodes per pixel, not per leaf.
\n    // wgpu has no sampler LOD bias and the sampler is shared with unbiased batches, so it goes on
\n    // this sample. Clutter's tint is white and its vertex colour the MCSH grey, so `* vo.color`
\n    // reproduces Bevy's fold.
\n    if (m.clutter_fade.w > 0.5) {
\n#ifdef VERTEX_UVS_A
\n        var biased = textureSampleBias(
\n            pbr_bindings::base_color_texture,
\n            pbr_bindings::base_color_sampler,
\n            view.mip_bias + DETAIL_DOODAD_LOD_BIAS,
\n#ifdef VERTEX_COLORS
\n        biased = biased * vo.color;
\n#endif
\n        base_color = biased;
\n#endif
\n    if (clipped) {
\n        discard;
\n    // The clutter distance fade, the reference's stage-1 ramp: u = (z_eye − 52.5)/17.5 by a
\n    // camera-space texgen (`0x6b2b80`), so the boundary is a view plane, not a sphere; the ramp is
\n    // a bilinear read of the 64-texel table `4·(63 − col)` (`0x6b2320`). It multiplies the alpha
\n    // the cutout tests (ALPHAREF `detailDoodadAlpha` = 128).
\n    if (m.clutter_fade.w > 0.5) {
\n        let z_eye = -(view.view_from_world * vec4<f32>(in.world_position.xyz, 1.0)).z;
\n        let u = (z_eye - m.clutter_fade.x) / max(m.clutter_fade.y - m.clutter_fade.x, 0.001);
\n        let ramp = clamp((254.0 - 256.0 * u) / 255.0, 0.0, 252.0 / 255.0);
\n        base_color.a = base_color.a * ramp;
\n    // Stage 1 (`0x70b740` binds a stage per texture of the unit): its alpha joins the stage-0
\n    // alpha the cutout reads (the blend's is `faded_alpha`, below); its colour combines after the light (below).
\n    let stage1_on = m.stage1.x > 0.5;
\n    let stage1_preset = u32(m.stage1.y);
\n    let tex0_alpha = base_color.a;
\n    var tex1 = vec4<f32>(1.0);
\n    if (stage1_on) {
\n        tex1 = textureSampleBias(stage1_texture, stage1_sampler, in.env_uv, view.mip_bias);
\n        base_color.a = stage_alpha(stage1_preset, base_color.a, tex1.a);
\n    // The MeshTag (mesh_tag.rs): bit 31 = highlight, bit 30 = interior fog; payload bits 0-5 = the
\n    // fade alpha (a zero payload is untagged, opaque), 19-29 = the rig slot, 6-13 = the ground
\n    // shade (0 lit, 255 MCSH-shadowed) or, on an interior-prop material, 6-18 = the SH-probe slot.
\n    let interior_prop = m.model_flags.z > 0.5 && m.model_flags.x < 0.5;
\n    let raw_tag = mesh_functions::get_tag(in.instance_index);
\n    let highlighted = (raw_tag & 0x80000000u) != 0u;
\n    let interior_fogged = (raw_tag & 0x40000000u) != 0u;
\n    let fade_tag = raw_tag & 0x3fffffffu;
\n    let alpha6 = f32(fade_tag & 0x3fu) / 63.0;
\n    var obj_fade = select(alpha6, 1.0, fade_tag == 0u);
\n#ifdef WOW_MERGED_FADE
\n    // A merged blob's per-vertex fade composes where the tag fade does, so it feathers the same.
\n    obj_fade = obj_fade * in.merged_fade;
\n#endif
\n    // The body tint (an aura colouring the whole model), by rig slot, 0 = identity: the material
\n    // ambient+diffuse colour (gx SetState(1), GL_COLOR_MATERIAL), so it multiplies the light sum
\n    // inside the clamp, never the emission.
\n    let tint_word = wow_light.rig_tint[(fade_tag >> 19u) & 0x7ffu];
\n    let inst_tint = select(
\n        vec3<f32>(
\n            f32((tint_word >> 16u) & 0xffu),
\n            f32((tint_word >> 8u) & 0xffu),
\n            f32(tint_word & 0xffu),
\n        vec3<f32>(1.0),
\n        tint_word == 0u,
\n    // The blend twin re-applies its source's cutout: the reference scales ALPHAREF with the fade,
\n    // so the cutoff stays tex.a < 224/255 on the unfaded alpha. Only for a source batch that
\n    // alpha-tests (bit 10): ALPHAREF keys on the stored blend mode.
\n    if ((u32(m.clutter_fade.z) & 1024u) != 0u && base_color.a < VANILLA_ALPHA_KEY) {
\n        discard;
\n    // The depth-prime twin (`M2UseZFill`) masks colour writes, so only the discards above shape its
\n    // depth. No early return: naga's MSL backend miscompiles the dead tail ("redefinition of
\n    // '_tmp'").
\n    // The blended alpha is the stage chain on the instance alpha, the diffuse (`0x70c73a`, c28.w):
\n    // stage 0 combines it with the texel by its preset's alpha op, so an opaque batch's preset 0
\n    // (`0x811f8c`) blends by the fade alone and the texel's alpha never reaches the frame. Stage 1
\n    // follows on that. `m.stage1.z` is the stage-0 preset + 1, 0 for a batch with none.
\n    var faded_alpha = base_color.a * obj_fade;
\n    if (m.stage1.z > 0.5) {
\n        faded_alpha = stage_alpha(u32(m.stage1.z) - 1u, obj_fade, tex0_alpha);
\n        if (stage1_on) {
\n            faded_alpha = stage_alpha(stage1_preset, faded_alpha, tex1.a);
\n    let base = alpha_discard(pbr_input.material, base_color);
\n    // --- Lighting --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
\n    let is_clutter = m.clutter_fade.w > 0.5;
\n    let L = -normalize(wow_light.light_sun.xyz);
\n    // `wow_normalize`: an authored zero normal reaches here on the unskinned lane.
\n    let n_m2 = wow_normalize(pbr_input.world_normal);
\n    // Bevy negates `world_normal` on back faces of double-sided materials (foliage, every WMO
\n    // face); the reference never enables GL_LIGHT_MODEL_TWO_SIDE (`0x59ce30`), so undo it.
\n    let n_lit = select(-n_m2, n_m2, is_front);
\n    let ndotl = max(dot(n_lit, L), 0.0);
\n    let lit_nl = clamp(wow_light.light_ambient.rgb + wow_light.light_diffuse.rgb * ndotl, vec3<f32>(0.0), vec3<f32>(1.0));
\n    // The order-2 SH basis, shared by the exterior lobe and the interior probes.
\n    let quad = vec4<f32>(n_lit.x * n_lit.y, n_lit.y * n_lit.z, n_lit.z * n_lit.z, n_lit.x * n_lit.z);
\n    let n1 = vec4<f32>(n_lit, 1.0);
\n    let x2y2 = n_lit.x * n_lit.x - n_lit.y * n_lit.y;
\n    // Exterior doodads and entities: the header's `Model2.bls` lobe at the per-instance intensity
\n    // I, `[node+0xa4]` (animator targets 2.5 lit and 0.5 shadowed, `0x69e4ad`/`0x69e280`; 1.0
\n    // indoors, `0x69e36b`). `sun_scale.x` picks the family:
\n    //   ≥ 0.85: an entity M2, 2.5 mixed toward 0.5 by the tag's shade byte (ramped like `0x69e770`)
\n    //   0.5..0.85: a doodad (ADT MDDF or WMO MODD, both `CMapDoodadDef`): 1.0, never 2.5
\n    //   < 0.5: a doodad on MCSH-shadowed ground: 0.5
\n    // Deviation: `min(I, 1)`. The reference bakes I into the SH unclamped (`0x71c4e0`), so a lit
\n    // entity commits ×2.5 there and ×1.0 here; lifting the cap takes sun-facing surfaces past 1.0.
\n    // `entity_shade::LIT_T` aims the lit ramp at 1.0 because of it: lift the cap and set `LIT_T`
\n    // back to 0.0 together.
\n    let inst_shade = select(f32((fade_tag >> 6u) & 0xffu) / 255.0, 0.0, interior_prop);
\n    let mat_shade = select(0.0, 1.0, m.sun_scale.x < 0.5);
\n    let shade_t = max(mat_shade, inst_shade);
\n    let mid_band = m.sun_scale.x >= 0.5 && m.sun_scale.x < 0.85;
\n    let intensity = min(select(mix(2.5, 0.5, shade_t), 1.0, mid_band), 1.0);
\n    // One `intensity` multiply covers every sun band (never I²); the c10 `.w` ambient does not
\n    // scale. `pack_model_core_rows` packs the same closed form.
\n    let sun_dc = wow_light.grade.yzw * intensity;
\n    let sun_lobe = vec3<f32>(
\n        wow_light.sh_c10_r.w + sun_dc.x
\n            + intensity
\n                * (dot(wow_light.sh_c10_r.xyz, n_lit) + dot(wow_light.sh_c13_r, quad)
\n                    + wow_light.sh_c16.x * x2y2),
\n        wow_light.sh_c10_g.w + sun_dc.y
\n            + intensity
\n                * (dot(wow_light.sh_c10_g.xyz, n_lit) + dot(wow_light.sh_c13_g, quad)
\n                    + wow_light.sh_c16.y * x2y2),
\n        wow_light.sh_c10_b.w + sun_dc.z
\n            + intensity
\n                * (dot(wow_light.sh_c10_b.xyz, n_lit) + dot(wow_light.sh_c13_b, quad)
\n                    + wow_light.sh_c16.z * x2y2),
\n    // Clamp the sum, never a term: the lobe's own ringing dips to −0.037·C near μ ≈ −0.53, and a
\n    // per-term clamp would erase it.
\n    let lit_doodad = clamp(sun_lobe, vec3<f32>(0.0), vec3<f32>(1.0));
\n    // WMO and clutter take the FFP N·L light with no terrain shade; the lobe needs the directional
\n    // light on (`light_sun.w`).
\n    let is_wmo = m.model_flags.x > 0.5;
\n    let is_interior = m.model_flags.z > 0.5;
\n    let use_doodad_shade = (wow_light.light_sun.w > 0.5) && !is_clutter && !is_wmo;
\n    let lit_exterior = select(lit_nl, lit_doodad, use_doodad_shade);
\n    // WMO interior groups (`groupFlags & 0x48 == 0`) by batch class (`tint.w`): INT (1) is unlit
\n    // `tex × MOCV`; TRANS (2) is the reference's two passes, lit × MOCV.a + unlit × (1 − MOCV.a),
\n    // as one lerp; EXT (0) is `lit_nl`. A WINDOW batch (MOMT 0x20) on the interior drawer lights
\n    // with ambient = diffuse = the Direct/Ambient midpoint, ambient +16/255 (`0x6d37e0`).
\n    var trans_a = 1.0;
\n#ifdef VERTEX_COLORS
\n    trans_a = in.color.a;
\n#endif
\n    let window_mid = 0.5 * (wow_light.light_ambient.rgb + wow_light.light_diffuse.rgb);
\n    let lit_window = clamp(
\n        window_mid + vec3<f32>(16.0 / 255.0) + window_mid * ndotl,
\n        vec3<f32>(0.0),
\n        vec3<f32>(1.0),
\n    let lit_int_base = select(lit_nl, lit_window, m.sidn.w > 0.5);
\n    var lit_wmo_interior = vec3<f32>(1.0);
\n    if (m.tint.w > 1.5) {
\n        lit_wmo_interior = mix(vec3<f32>(1.0), lit_int_base, trans_a);
\n    } else if (m.tint.w < 0.5) {
\n        lit_wmo_interior = lit_int_base;
\n    // Interior M2 props (WMO MODD doodads): the reference commits the prop's MODD colour through a
\n    // fixed-axis diffuse lobe plus its group's MOLR lights as an order-2 SH probe, folded at spawn
\n    // by `lighting::prop_probe_coeffs` and evaluated here per fragment (the reference: per vertex).
\n    // Its soft wrap (≈ 0.088·C side-on) is the reference's response, not a max(N·L, 0).
\n#ifdef WOW_MERGED_SLOT
\n    // A merged blob bakes the slot per vertex; its tag carries only fog and alpha.
\n    let probe = 7u * in.merged_slot;
\n#else
\n    let probe = 7u * ((fade_tag >> 6u) & 0x1fffu);
\n#endif
\n    let lit_m2_interior = clamp(
\n        vec3<f32>(
\n            dot(wow_light.prop_probes[probe + 0u], n1)
\n                + dot(wow_light.prop_probes[probe + 3u], quad)
\n                + wow_light.prop_probes[probe + 6u].x * x2y2,
\n            dot(wow_light.prop_probes[probe + 1u], n1)
\n                + dot(wow_light.prop_probes[probe + 4u], quad)
\n                + wow_light.prop_probes[probe + 6u].y * x2y2,
\n            dot(wow_light.prop_probes[probe + 2u], n1)
\n                + dot(wow_light.prop_probes[probe + 5u], quad)
\n                + wow_light.prop_probes[probe + 6u].z * x2y2,
\n        vec3<f32>(0.0),
\n        vec3<f32>(1.0),
\n    let lit_interior = select(lit_m2_interior, lit_wmo_interior, is_wmo);
\n    // The authored-rig lane (`ShadeSel::Rig`, glue scenes): the scene's lights are folded into
\n    // probe slot 0 of the material's own buffer, which `lit_m2_interior` already evaluated (tag 0).
\n    let is_rig = m.sun_scale.x >= 1.5;
\n    let lit = select(select(lit_exterior, lit_interior, is_interior), lit_m2_interior, is_rig);
\n    // Gamma-space albedo: lighting runs on the authored byte values. `m.tint` plus its mat-anim
\n    // delta is the animated M2Color tint.
\n    let anim_tint = m.tint.rgb + wow_light.matanim[u32(m.anim_slots.y)].xyz;
\n    let albedo = base.rgb * anim_tint;
\n    // An unlit batch replaces the lit path: fullbright, with only the highlight added (below).
\n    let is_emissive = m.model_flags.w > 0.5;
\n    // SIDN night glow: the emissive × the night fraction (ramping 20:30→21:30, 06:00→07:00), a
\n    // GL_EMISSION term inside the clamped lit sum, on lit lanes only.
\n    var sidn_w = 1.0;
\n    if (is_interior && is_wmo) {
\n        if (m.tint.w > 1.5) {
\n            sidn_w = trans_a; // TRANS: weighted by its lit pass
\n        } else if (m.tint.w > 0.5) {
\n            sidn_w = 0.0; // INT: unlit, so no emission
\n    let sidn_e = m.sidn.rgb * (wow_light.grade.x * sidn_w);
\n    let point_diffuse = in.point_lit;
\n    // The hover/target highlight (tag bit 31): the scene's committed ambient
\n    // (`0x614576`-`0x6145bd`), added to the batch colour inside the final clamp, lit or unlit
\n    // (`c29`). Sampled live, where the reference holds the value sampled when the highlight
\n    // began: a unit's tag has no slot to hold a colour, and the ambient moves slowly.
\n    let highlight = select(vec3<f32>(0.0), wow_light.light_ambient.rgb, highlighted);
\n    // The FFP combine: the light sum (lit, point lights, emission) clamps first and the texture
\n    // modulates it, `tex × clamp(C·sum + emission)`, with C the GL_COLOR_MATERIAL colour (MOCV on
\n    // WMO, the body tint on M2). The WMO branch divides Bevy's MOCV fold back out, guarded; a dim
\n    // channel's product is ~0 either way.
\n    var lit_rgb: vec3<f32>;
\n#ifdef VERTEX_COLORS
\n    if (is_wmo) {
\n        let vc = in.color.rgb;
\n        let primary = clamp(
\n            vc * (lit + point_diffuse) + sidn_e + highlight,
\n            vec3<f32>(0.0),
\n            vec3<f32>(1.0),
\n        let tex_rgb = base.rgb / max(vc, vec3<f32>(1.0 / 255.0));
\n        lit_rgb = tex_rgb * m.tint.rgb * primary;
\n        if (is_interior && m.tint.w > 0.5 && m.tint.w < 1.5) {
\n            // INT: the reference's interior pixel shader, `tex·MOCV.rgb·(1 + 4·MOCV.a)` with only
\n            // the framebuffer's final clamp.
\n            lit_rgb = clamp(
\n                tex_rgb * m.tint.rgb * vc * (1.0 + 4.0 * trans_a),
\n                vec3<f32>(0.0),
\n                vec3<f32>(1.0),
\n    } else {
\n        // An M2: the body tint multiplies the light terms as MOCV does above. A WMO surface has
\n        // no tint slot, so the WMO branch leaves it out.
\n        let primary = clamp(
\n            inst_tint * (lit + point_diffuse) + sidn_e + highlight,
\n            vec3<f32>(0.0),
\n            vec3<f32>(1.0),
\n        lit_rgb = albedo * primary;
\n#else
\n    // A WMO batch without MOCV lands here too; its tint slot is the identity slot 0.
\n    let primary = clamp(
\n        inst_tint * (lit + point_diffuse) + sidn_e + highlight,
\n        vec3<f32>(0.0),
\n        vec3<f32>(1.0),
\n    lit_rgb = albedo * primary;
\n#endif
\n    // The unlit path: an M2's unlit program outputs `c28 + c29` (`0x70c663`-`0x70c693` fold the
\n    // tint·M2Color term into `c29` beside the highlight), so the texel modulates
\n    // `clamp(C·tint + highlight)`, C the M2Color. A WMO keeps the plain modulate.
\n    var unlit_rgb = albedo * inst_tint;
\n    if (!is_wmo) {
\n#ifdef VERTEX_COLORS
\n        // The constant M2Color rides the vertex colour, which Bevy folded into `base`.
\n        let unlit_c = in.color.rgb * anim_tint;
\n        let unlit_tex = base.rgb / max(in.color.rgb, vec3<f32>(1.0 / 255.0));
\n#else
\n        let unlit_c = anim_tint;
\n        let unlit_tex = base.rgb;
\n#endif
\n        let unlit_sum = unlit_c * inst_tint + highlight;
\n        unlit_rgb = unlit_tex * clamp(unlit_sum, vec3<f32>(0.0), vec3<f32>(1.0));
\n    var rgb = select(lit_rgb, unlit_rgb, is_emissive);
\n    // An M2 Mod or Mod2x batch draws the bare texel: the reference zeroes its tint·M2Color term and
\n    // forces the primary colour to the blend identity (`0x70c507`/`0x70c5b8`), so neither the
\n    // animated M2Color nor the body tint reaches it. Its alpha still does, through the lerp below.
\n    let is_mod = (u32(m.clutter_fade.z) & 128u) != 0u;
\n    let is_mod2x = (u32(m.clutter_fade.z) & 256u) != 0u;
\n    if ((is_mod || is_mod2x) && !is_wmo) {
\n        rgb = base.rgb;
\n    // Stage 1 combines with the stage-0 result, the lit texel, before the fog.
\n    if (stage1_on) {
\n        // The diffuse alpha is the batch and instance alpha, the shader's `obj_fade`.
\n        rgb = stage1_rgb(stage1_preset, rgb, tex1, obj_fade);
\n    // Linear fog by planar eye depth, as in terrain.wgsl. Per-batch colour policy (`clutter_fade.z`
\n    // bits 4-6, the M2 state setter `0x70baf0`): 0 scene, 1 black (additive), 2 white (Mod),
\n    // 3 grey (Mod2x), 4 unfogged (render flag 0x02). Tag bit 30, not the static `model_flags.z`,
\n    // selects the interior triple: WMO content by the per-group `[0xca7f00]` gate on the pushes
\n    // `0x6b5190`/`0x6b62e0`, an entity M2 by its node's classification (`0x71c110`, `[node+0xc]`).
\n    var fog_color = wow_light.fog_color;
\n    var fog_span = wow_light.fog_params.xy;
\n    if (interior_fogged) {
\n        fog_color = wow_light.wmo_fog_color;
\n        fog_span = wow_light.wmo_fog_params.xy;
\n    let fog_policy = (u32(m.clutter_fade.z) >> 4u) & 7u;
\n    if (fog_color.w > 0.5 && fog_policy != 4u) {
\n        let eye_z = -(view.view_from_world * vec4<f32>(in.world_position.xyz, 1.0)).z;
\n        let denom = max(fog_span.y - fog_span.x, 0.001);
\n        let factor = clamp((fog_span.y - eye_z) / denom, 0.0, 1.0);
\n        var fog_rgb = fog_color.xyz;
\n        if (fog_policy == 1u) { fog_rgb = vec3<f32>(0.0); }
\n        else if (fog_policy == 2u) { fog_rgb = vec3<f32>(1.0); }
\n        else if (fog_policy == 3u) { fog_rgb = vec3<f32>(0.50196078); }
\n        rgb = mix(fog_rgb, rgb, factor);
\n    var out: WowFragOut;
\n    // Output alpha is `faded_alpha`. Opaque intent (`clutter_fade.z` bit 3) pins it to 1: a no-op
\n    // under correct pipeline state, and a guard for macOS/Metal with an extra camera, where an
\n    // opaque draw can bind a blending pipeline and show the BLP's garbage alpha.
\n    let opaque_intent = (u32(m.clutter_fade.z) & 8u) != 0u;
\n    // Additive (`clutter_fade.z` bit 2, the bit `specialize` keys the (ONE, ONE) blend on): the
\n    // alpha weight folds into the colour here, in gamma, as the reference weights its source.
\n    let is_additive = (u32(m.clutter_fade.z) & 4u) != 0u;
\n    var out_rgb = rgb;
\n    if (is_additive) {
\n        out_rgb = out_rgb * faded_alpha;
\n    // Mod (bit 7) and Mod2x (bit 8) read no source alpha, so the fade rides the colour as in the
\n    // reference: texenv preset 5, `mix(prev.rgb, tex.rgb, prev.a)`, with the primary colour forced
\n    // to the blend identity (white, or 0.5 grey for Mod2x) and prev.a the instance alpha. The fog
\n    // above commutes with this because its white and grey are that identity.
\n    if (is_mod || is_mod2x) {
\n        let identity = select(vec3<f32>(1.0), vec3<f32>(0.5), is_mod2x);
\n        out_rgb = mix(identity, out_rgb, obj_fade);
\n    // Raw gamma out: blending happens in gamma like the reference's byte framebuffer; the frame
\n    // decodes once, in the FFXGlow combine.
\n    out.color = vec4<f32>(out_rgb, select(faded_alpha, 1.0, opaque_intent));
\n    return out;
shaders/wdl.wgsl// WDL distant terrain: the coarse horizon hulls the reference draws past the detailed tiles,
\n// unlit, untextured, white vertex diffuse fogged with the scene's fog colour. The hull emitter
\n// `0x6bd780` sets its own fog pair, start 0 and end 1.0 (`0x6bd7ae`-`0x6bd7c8`), so beyond one
\n// yard the hull is the flat fog colour: a silhouette against the unfogged sky.
\n// The band is a backdrop, not the far half of a shared clip plane. The reference's far-band pass
\n// (`0x6841a0`, projection at `0x6842f2`) uses near `farclip - 33` (`[0x8101b0]`) and the depth
\n// range `[0.955, 0.96]` (`[0x80febc]` = 0.96, `[0x80fec4]` = 0.005): the band overlaps the detailed
\n// world by 33 yd, closing the seam, and stays behind all of it. On Bevy's infinite reverse-Z
\n// (depth = near / eye_z) that range becomes a clamp just below `near / farclip`, the farthest
\n// depth the detailed world keeps (it discards past the wall), still in front of the sky's 0.0.
\n#import bevy_pbr::{
\n    mesh_functions,
\n    forward_io::Vertex,
\n    view_transformations::{position_world_to_clip, view_z_to_depth_ndc},
\n    mesh_view_bindings::view,
\n/// How far the band reaches inside the far-clip wall: the reference's far-band near plane
\n/// `farclip - 33.0` (`[0x8101b0]`, about one WDL outer cell).
\nconst WDL_OVERLAP: f32 = 33.0;
\n/// Keeps the band strictly behind a world fragment exactly at the wall (`GreaterEqual` passes a
\n/// tie); multiplicative, so it never crosses zero into the sky.
\nconst WDL_DEPTH_PUSH: f32 = 0.999;
\n// The shared global light (`lighting::global_light`), mirrored up to the rows WDL reads. Rows 4
\n// and 5 are the scene fog block, right by construction: the horizon band is never inside a WMO.
\nstruct WowLight {
\n    _light_ambient: vec4<f32>, // 0
\n    _light_diffuse: vec4<f32>, // 1
\n    _light_sun: vec4<f32>,     // 2
\n    _light_spec: vec4<f32>,    // 3
\n    fog_color: vec4<f32>,      // 4 rgb = Light.dbc row 7 (gamma 0..1); w = enable (>0.5 ⇒ blend)
\n    fog_params: vec4<f32>,     // 5 xy = scene fog start/end (unread); w = farclip wall (0 = off)
\n@group(#{MATERIAL_BIND_GROUP}) @binding(90) var<storage, read> w: WowLight;
\nstruct WdlVsOut {
\n    @builtin(position) clip_position: vec4<f32>,
\n    @location(0) world_position: vec4<f32>,
\nstruct WdlFsOut {
\n    @location(0) color: vec4<f32>,
\n    @builtin(frag_depth) depth: f32,
\n@vertex
\nfn vertex(in: Vertex) -> WdlVsOut {
\n    var out: WdlVsOut;
\n    let world_from_local = mesh_functions::get_world_from_local(in.instance_index);
\n    out.world_position =
\n        mesh_functions::mesh_position_local_to_world(world_from_local, vec4<f32>(in.position, 1.0));
\n    out.clip_position = position_world_to_clip(out.world_position.xyz);
\n    return out;
\n@fragment
\nfn fragment(in: WdlVsOut) -> WdlFsOut {
\n    // Planar eye-z, not radial: the band's near plane is a projection plane.
\n    let eye_z = -(view.view_from_world * vec4<f32>(in.world_position.xyz, 1.0)).z;
\n    let farclip = w.fog_params.w;
\n    // The near plane is `farclip - 33`, not the wall: the overlap closes the coarse-vs-fine seam.
\n    if (farclip > 0.0 && eye_z < farclip - WDL_OVERLAP) {
\n        discard;
\n    // White vertex diffuse under the hull's own fog pair, saturated beyond one yard: the flat fog
\n    // colour, never the scene fog distances. With fog off the reference shows the bare white hull.
\n    var rgb = vec3<f32>(1.0);
\n    if (w.fog_color.w > 0.5) {
\n        rgb = w.fog_color.xyz;
\n    var out: WdlFsOut;
\n    // Raw gamma out; the frame decodes once, in the FFXGlow combine.
\n    out.color = vec4<f32>(rgb, 1.0);
\n    // The depth clamp. `view_z_to_depth_ndc` takes view-space z, negative in front of the camera,
\n    // so the wall is at `-farclip`.
\n    var depth = in.clip_position.z;
\n    if (farclip > 0.0) {
\n        depth = min(depth, view_z_to_depth_ndc(-farclip) * WDL_DEPTH_PUSH);
\n    out.depth = depth;
\n    return out;
shaders/liquid.wgsl// Liquid shader, one arm per reference liquid renderer:
\n//   ADT MCLQ river/ocean (`0x6851b0`/`0x685010`): `ocean0_s.bls`, the depth swatch on stage 0 and
\n//     the animated sheet on stage 1; the only arm with a depth ramp.
\n//   WMO MLIQ water (`0x6b62e0` category 0), split on `MOGP.flags & 0x48`: exterior `0x6b6630`
\n//     binds `MapObjExtWater0.bls`, interior `0x6b6420` is fixed-function and unlit.
\n//   Magma/slime (`0x6b68f0` WMO, `0x68dca0` ADT): the sheet is the opaque body.
\n// The ADT combine, `Shaders\Pixel\ocean0_s.bls` (0.25 is the program's own `PARAM`):
\n//   rgb   = primary·colorTex.rgb + detail.rgb + (secondary + 0.25)·detail.a
\n//   alpha = colorTex.a
\n// colorTex is the depth swatch off the zone's `Light.dbc` water bands (IntBand 16/17 river/lake,
\n// 14/15 ocean), rebuilt every frame (`0x680b90`, refill `0x58acd0`); detail is the `lake_a` or
\n// `ocean_h` frame, near-black RGB and the ripple in alpha, which its authored mips fade with
\n// distance, so the sampler's mips and anisotropy matter; primary is the lit default white vertex
\n// (`glColorMaterial`); secondary is the sun sheen.
\n// The ADT water alpha is the swatch's own: the `0xc7fbc0` LUT texture binds only behind
\n// `[0xc800ec]` (`0x685244`-`0x685257`), which never holds one (its one store, `0x68c7f8`, is 0).
\n// Deviation: this is the `specular`/`pixelShaders` = 1 leg the reference install runs; both CVars
\n// (`0x6886a0`/`0x688712`) default to 0, where water has no program, no specular, a plain ADD
\n// combine and no blend. An active ARB program bypasses the texture environment.
\n// Culling is off for every kind: all four reference liquid passes disable GL_CULL_FACE. Water
\n// blends with depth write off; magma and slime are opaque and write depth. Output is raw gamma.
\n#import bevy_pbr::{
\n    mesh_functions,
\n    forward_io::Vertex,
\n    view_transformations::position_world_to_clip,
\n    mesh_view_bindings::{view, globals},
\n@group(#{MATERIAL_BIND_GROUP}) @binding(100) var frames: texture_2d_array<f32>;
\n@group(#{MATERIAL_BIND_GROUP}) @binding(101) var frames_samp: sampler;
\nstruct LiquidParams {
\n    // x = fullbright (magma/slime); y = ocean swatch; z = interior fog; w = sun-sheen shininess.
\n    kind: vec4<f32>,
\n    // x = renderer (`LiquidPath`): 0 = ADT MCLQ, 1 = WMO exterior, 2 = WMO interior; yzw reserved.
\n    path: vec4<f32>,
\n    // y = frame count; z = scroll flag (WMO magma/slime only, liquid nibbles 6/7); w = clock
\n    // enable (0 on a deterministic run).
\n    anim: vec4<f32>,
\n@group(#{MATERIAL_BIND_GROUP}) @binding(102) var<uniform> w: LiquidParams;
\n// The prefix of the shared global light (`lighting::global_light`); it must match row for row.
\nstruct WowLight {
\n    light_ambient: vec4<f32>,      // 0  rgb = ambient; w = Mod2x scale
\n    light_diffuse: vec4<f32>,      // 1  rgb = sun diffuse; w = clamp flag
\n    light_sun: vec4<f32>,          // 2  xyz = sun travel direction (to-light = −xyz)
\n    light_spec: vec4<f32>,         // 3  rgb = row-9 specular colour; w = terrain shininess, unread
\n    fog_color: vec4<f32>,          // 4  rgb = scene fog (block 1, gamma 0..1); w = enable (>0.5)
\n    fog_params: vec4<f32>,         // 5  x = start yd; y = end yd; w = the farclip wall
\n    _sh: array<vec4<f32>, 6>,      // 6-11  model SH coefficients, unread here
\n    _sh_c16: vec4<f32>,            // 12
\n    water_river: array<vec4<f32>, 2>, // 13-14 river/lake shallow, deep (IntBand 16/17); w = alpha
\n    water_ocean: array<vec4<f32>, 2>, // 15-16 ocean shallow, deep (IntBand 14/15); w = alpha
\n    _grade: vec4<f32>,             // 17
\n    wmo_fog_color: vec4<f32>,      // 18 rgb = interior fog (block 2); w = enable
\n    wmo_fog_params: vec4<f32>,     // 19 x = start yd; y = end yd
\n@group(#{MATERIAL_BIND_GROUP}) @binding(90) var<storage, read> wow_light: WowLight;
\nstruct LiquidVsOut {
\n    @builtin(position) clip_position: vec4<f32>,
\n    @location(0) world_position: vec4<f32>,
\n    @location(1) world_normal: vec3<f32>,
\n    @location(2) uv: vec2<f32>,
\n    @location(3) depth: f32,
\n    // The sun sheen, per vertex and interpolated, as the reference's fixed-function stage does.
\n    @location(4) secondary_vtx: vec3<f32>,
\n    // A WMO interior pool's `MOMT.diffColor`, as its reference vertex carries; white elsewhere.
\n    @location(5) vcolor: vec4<f32>,
\n    // `MeshTag` bit 30: the room's per-frame interior-fog gate, the reference's `[0xca7f00]`.
\n    @location(6) @interpolate(flat) room_fog: u32,
\n// Sun sheen (`secondary`): the Blinn highlight `light_spec.rgb · (N·H)^shininess`.
\nfn sun_sheen(world_normal: vec3<f32>, world_pos: vec3<f32>) -> vec3<f32> {
\n    let n = normalize(world_normal);
\n    let to_light = -normalize(wow_light.light_sun.xyz);
\n    // Local viewer, per vertex: the reference sets `GL_LIGHT_MODEL_LOCAL_VIEWER = 1` at `0x59cf89`.
\n    let to_view = normalize(view.world_position.xyz - world_pos);
\n    let half_v = normalize(to_light + to_view);
\n    let ndoth = max(dot(n, half_v), 0.0);
\n    // No `N·L > 0` specular gate: the sun stays between +20° and +37° (`DayNight::SetDirection`),
\n    // so N·L on the flat up normal is always > 0. Shininess is water's own (6.0, `[0x8102e8]`) and
\n    // material specular is white (`SetRenderState(3, 0xffffffff)`). The reference's specular light
\n    // colour (`CGLight+0x48` to `glLightfv(GL_SPECULAR)`) is not pinned; row 9 stands in for it.
\n    return wow_light.light_spec.rgb * pow(ndoth, max(w.kind.w, 1.0));
\nfn anim_time() -> f32 {
\n    return w.anim.w * globals.time;
\n// The 24 fps flip, 30 frames over 1.25 s (`0x68aac0`), floored to a whole frame.
\nfn frame_layer() -> i32 {
\n    return i32(floor(anim_time() * 24.0) % max(w.anim.y, 1.0));
\nfn apply_scroll(uv: vec2<f32>) -> vec2<f32> {
\n    // Magma/slime scroll (liquid nibbles 6/7): the reference's stage-0 texture matrix (`0x6b68f0`,
\n    // pushed at `0x6b6ae3`) translates v by `fmod(t, 10) · 0.1` (rate `[0x801620]`, period
\n    // `[0x80e5a0]`), continuously; its phase is machine uptime, so only rate and period match.
\n    // REPEAT wrapping hides the reset.
\n    return vec2<f32>(uv.x, uv.y + w.anim.z * fract(anim_time() / 10.0));
\n// Planar eye-Z GL_LINEAR fog in gamma space, as terrain.wgsl; GL_FOG defaults on (`0x593bf0`) and
\n// no liquid pass turns it off. Block 1 (`+0x70/74/78`) is the scene fog (`0x66ff20`); block 2
\n// (`+0x80/84/88`) is the interior haze, eased toward the MFOG or zone target over about 4 s
\n// (`0x6cf054`). Only the WMO geometry pass (`0x6b51d9`/`0x6b51ea`) and the WMO liquid pass
\n// (`0x6b6323` to `0x6b6342`) submit block 2, under the room gate `[0xca7f00]`: `w.kind.z` is its
\n// static half (`MOGI & 0x48`), `room_fog` the per-frame half.
\nfn apply_fog(rgb: vec3<f32>, world_pos: vec3<f32>, room_fog: u32) -> vec3<f32> {
\n    var fog_color = wow_light.fog_color;
\n    var fog_span = wow_light.fog_params.xy;
\n    if (w.kind.z > 0.5 && room_fog != 0u) {
\n        fog_color = wow_light.wmo_fog_color;
\n        fog_span = wow_light.wmo_fog_params.xy;
\n    if (fog_color.w <= 0.5) {
\n        return rgb;
\n    let eye_z = -(view.view_from_world * vec4<f32>(world_pos, 1.0)).z;
\n    let denom = max(fog_span.y - fog_span.x, 0.001);
\n    let factor = clamp((fog_span.y - eye_z) / denom, 0.0, 1.0);
\n    return mix(fog_color.xyz, rgb, factor);
\n@vertex
\nfn vertex(in: Vertex) -> LiquidVsOut {
\n    var out: LiquidVsOut;
\n    let world_from_local = mesh_functions::get_world_from_local(in.instance_index);
\n    out.world_position =
\n        mesh_functions::mesh_position_local_to_world(world_from_local, vec4<f32>(in.position, 1.0));
\n    out.clip_position = position_world_to_clip(out.world_position.xyz);
\n    out.world_normal = mesh_functions::mesh_normal_local_to_world(in.normal, in.instance_index);
\n    out.uv = in.uv;
\n#ifdef VERTEX_COLORS
\n    out.vcolor = in.color;
\n#else
\n    out.vcolor = vec4<f32>(1.0);
\n#endif
\n    // Depth coordinate V (0..1) in UV1.x: the swatch row on ADT water, the alpha ramp on WMO.
\n    out.depth = in.uv_b.x;
\n    out.secondary_vtx = sun_sheen(out.world_normal, out.world_position.xyz);
\n    // ADT surfaces carry no `MeshTag`, so they take the scene fog.
\n    out.room_fog = mesh_functions::get_tag(in.instance_index) & 0x40000000u;
\n    return out;
\n// ── The ADT depth swatch ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
\n// `0x68a830` fills an 8×64 texture, each row the same across its 8 columns, with an exact
\n// byte-space integer accumulator, `row(i) = c0 + floor(i * (c1 - c0) / 64)` for i = 0..63, so
\n// row 63 stops short of the deep endpoint. On the ocean (selector 0) the last row's HSV value is
\n// scaled by 0.9 (`0x68aa13`, `[0x8102ec]`), which `floor(0.9 * byte)` reproduces within 1/255,
\n// and its alpha is forced to 255 (`0x7bbec0`/`0x7bbec8`). Sampling is LINEAR, no mip, clamped
\n// (flags `0x201`), so V maps to texel `V*64 - 0.5` and the ocean darkening ramps over the last
\n// 1/64 of V. The WMO arms use the 256-entry ramp `0xca7f10` instead, which a plain lerp
\n// reproduces.
\nfn swatch_row(shallow: vec4<f32>, deep: vec4<f32>, i: f32, ocean: bool) -> vec4<f32> {
\n    // RGB endpoints are bytes already (`0x68a8fb`/`0x68a902`), so they round back exactly; alpha
\n    // endpoints are `LightParams` floats the reference quantizes with `floor(v*255)`.
\n    let c0 = vec4<f32>(round(shallow.rgb * 255.0), floor(shallow.w * 255.0));
\n    let c1 = vec4<f32>(round(deep.rgb * 255.0), floor(deep.w * 255.0));
\n    let row = c0 + floor(i * (c1 - c0) / 64.0);
\n    if ocean && i >= 63.0 {
\n        return vec4<f32>(floor(row.rgb * 0.9), 255.0) / 255.0;
\n    return row / 255.0;
\n/// The swatch sampled at depth coord `v`, LINEAR across the two rows it falls between.
\nfn swatch_at(shallow: vec4<f32>, deep: vec4<f32>, v: f32, ocean: bool) -> vec4<f32> {
\n    let t = clamp(v * 64.0 - 0.5, 0.0, 63.0);
\n    let i0 = floor(t);
\n    return mix(
\n        swatch_row(shallow, deep, i0, ocean),
\n        swatch_row(shallow, deep, min(i0 + 1.0, 63.0), ocean),
\n@fragment
\nfn fragment(in: LiquidVsOut) -> @location(0) vec4<f32> {
\n    // The far-clip wall, as terrain and models: discard beyond `fog_params.w` (0 disables it).
\n    if (wow_light.fog_params.w > 0.0) {
\n        let clip_z = -(view.view_from_world * vec4<f32>(in.world_position.xyz, 1.0)).z;
\n        if (clip_z > wow_light.fog_params.w) {
\n            discard;
\n    // The animated frame; `view.mip_bias` is the render-scale LOD compensation, 0 at native.
\n    let detail = textureSampleBias(
\n        frames,
\n        frames_samp,
\n        apply_scroll(in.uv),
\n        frame_layer(),
\n        view.mip_bias,
\n    // Magma/slime: the sheet is the opaque body, unmodulated (the ADT vertex has no colour, the WMO
\n    // one is `0xffffffff`) and unlit (lighting off on both paths), but fogged.
\n    if (w.kind.x > 0.5) {
\n        return vec4<f32>(apply_fog(detail.rgb, in.world_position.xyz, in.room_fog), 1.0);
\n    // V, from the authored depth byte CPU-side: clamp(byte/42) on river/lake (LUT `0xc81768`,
\n    // `0x68d790`, saturating near 5 yd), clamp(byte/255) on ocean (LUT `0xc7fcd8`,
\n    // `0x68d690`), both built in `0x68c4c0`. One V indexes colour and alpha alike.
\n    let depth = clamp(in.depth, 0.0, 1.0);
\n    var shallow = wow_light.water_river[0];
\n    var deep = wow_light.water_river[1];
\n    if (w.kind.y > 0.5) {
\n        shallow = wow_light.water_ocean[0];
\n        deep = wow_light.water_ocean[1];
\n    // ---- The WMO water arms: opacity is the per-vertex authored byte through the zone's linear
\n    // alpha ramp, carried in `in.depth`.
\n    let vtx_alpha = mix(shallow.w, deep.w, depth);
\n    if (w.path.x > 1.5) {
\n        // ---- WMO interior (`0x6b6420`): fixed-function whatever the CVars (`[0xc9607c]` unread),
\n        // lighting off (`0x0e = 0`), fog on (`0x0f = 1`), combine preset `(0x1f, 3)`:
\n        //     rgb = clamp(Cf + Ct)      alpha = clamp(Af + At)
\n        // Cf is the pool's raw `MOMT.diffColor`; the vertex has no normal, so no sun and no sheen.
\n        // Preset 3 is `GL_ADD` through `GL_COMBINE` on both channels (`COMBINE_ALPHA` at
\n        // `0x85c2fc`), so the ripple adds to the pool's opacity rather than multiplying it.
\n        let body = clamp(in.vcolor.rgb + detail.rgb, vec3<f32>(0.0), vec3<f32>(1.0));
\n        return vec4<f32>(
\n            apply_fog(body, in.world_position.xyz, in.room_fog),
\n            clamp(vtx_alpha + detail.a, 0.0, 1.0),
\n    if (w.path.x > 0.5) {
\n        // ---- WMO exterior (`0x6b6630`): `Shaders\Pixel\MapObjExtWater0.bls` (bound `0x6b6654`),
\n        // the shader leg of the `[0xc9607c]` gate:
\n        //     rgb = primary.rgb + detail.rgb + secondary·detail.a      alpha = primary.a
\n        // No `+0.25`, which is the ADT program's own. Lighting is on (`0x0e` never set), so
\n        // primary = band · clamp(ambient + diffuse·max(N·L, 0)), the band one flat colour for
\n        // every nibble: the deep river row, `LightIntBand` sub-17 (`water_river[1]`), an immediate
\n        // at `0x6b66be`. A DayNight slot is not a sub: `0x6d64d0` moves sub-8 out to `+0x4c`, so
\n        // the kernel's slot 16 is sub-17.
\n        let n_ext = normalize(in.world_normal);
\n        let to_light_ext = -normalize(wow_light.light_sun.xyz);
\n        let primary_ext = clamp(
\n            wow_light.light_ambient.rgb + wow_light.light_diffuse.rgb
\n                * max(dot(n_ext, to_light_ext), 0.0),
\n            vec3<f32>(0.0),
\n            vec3<f32>(1.0),
\n        ) * deep.rgb;
\n        let rgb_ext = primary_ext + detail.rgb + in.secondary_vtx * detail.a;
\n        // Alpha is `fragment.color.primary` alone: the bound program bypasses the texture
\n        // environment, so the interior arm's `+ At` does not apply.
\n        return vec4<f32>(apply_fog(rgb_ext, in.world_position.xyz, in.room_fog), vtx_alpha);
\n    // The ADT arm. `primary`: the lit white vertex.
\n    let n = normalize(in.world_normal);
\n    let to_light = -normalize(wow_light.light_sun.xyz);
\n    let ndotl = max(dot(n, to_light), 0.0);
\n    let primary = clamp(
\n        wow_light.light_ambient.rgb + wow_light.light_diffuse.rgb * ndotl,
\n        vec3<f32>(0.0),
\n        vec3<f32>(1.0),
\n    let secondary = in.secondary_vtx;
\n    // colorTex: the stage-0 depth swatch.
\n    let swatch = swatch_at(shallow, deep, depth, w.kind.y > 0.5);
\n    // The `ocean0_s.bls` combine.
\n    var rgb = primary * swatch.rgb + detail.rgb + (secondary + vec3<f32>(0.25)) * detail.a;
\n    // `colorTex.a`, over the same V as the colour: deeper water is more opaque.
\n    let alpha = swatch.w;
\n    rgb = apply_fog(rgb, in.world_position.xyz, in.room_fog);
\n    // Raw gamma out; alpha blends in gamma space like the reference's bytes.
\n    return vec4<f32>(rgb, alpha);
